items.label: Strong Wolfe counterexample with sharp Hölder regularity
items.statement:
Theorem 1 (`thm:main`), with the regularity refinement in
`eq:counterexample-nonlipschitz`: in every dimension at least
two, the same strong-Wolfe counterexample has a globally one-half Hölder
Hessian and admits no larger exponent even on its initial sublevel.
items.title: Strong Wolfe counterexample with sharp Hölder regularity

items.label: Identity initialization with Hölder regularity
items.statement:
Corollary 2 (`cor:identity-initialization`): identity-initialized classical DFP fails to
converge in every dimension at least two even with a global one-half Hölder
Hessian and positive ordered uniform Hessian bounds.
items.title: Identity initialization with Hölder regularity

items.label: Planar convergence: weak Wolfe
items.statement:
Theorem 3 (`thm:planar-convergence`): arbitrary initial
positive-definite planar DFP data converge under the full fixed weak-Wolfe
range when the globally strongly convex C2 objective has locally Lipschitz
Hessian near its initial sublevel. Stationary termination is included through
constant continuation of the point sequence.
items.title: Planar convergence: weak Wolfe

items.label: Planar convergence: strong Wolfe
items.statement:
Paper-facing strong-Wolfe consequence of thm:planar-convergence:
strong curvature implies weak curvature after the descent property is
derived from Armijo and strong convexity.
items.title: Planar convergence: strong Wolfe

items.label: General secant degeneration
items.statement:
Lemma 11 (`lem:planar-degeneration`): positive-definite secant search matrices under
weak Wolfe degenerate along every nonconvergent planar strongly convex orbit.
The free coefficient is positive and bounded by adjacent step products, the
matrix sequence is bounded, and its smallest eigenvalue tends to zero.
items.title: General secant degeneration

items.label: Failure of global weak-Wolfe convergence
items.statement:
Main theorem: for every pair in the paper's Wolfe range, the
global weak-Wolfe convergence predicate is false.
items.title: Failure of global weak-Wolfe convergence

items.label: Failure of level-set global weak-Wolfe convergence
items.statement:
The same paper-range counterexample refutes the level-set version
of the fixed-coefficient global-convergence predicate.  The explicit
containment field is supplied by the Armijo/DFP descent bridge.
items.title: Failure of level-set global weak-Wolfe convergence

items.label: Strong Wolfe counterexample in every dimension
items.statement:
The paper-range strong-Wolfe counterexample is available in every
finite dimension `n` with `2 ≤ n`, while retaining the exact Hessian bounds
`(1 / 2, 3 / 2)`.
items.title: Strong Wolfe counterexample in every dimension

items.label: Identity-initialized strong Wolfe counterexample
items.statement:
For every pair in the paper's coefficient range and every
dimension `n ≥ 2`, the identity-initialization corollary has a genuine
matrix `InverseIteration` presentation.  The positive ordered Hessian bounds
and the `liminf` conclusion are generated automatically from the initial
positive-definite matrix.
items.title: Identity-initialized strong Wolfe counterexample

items.label: ofParabolicRecurrence
items.statement:
A positive real sequence tending to zero and satisfying
`ε (j + 1) = ε j - a * ε j ^ (p + 1) + O(ε j ^ (p + 2))` is asymptotic to
`(a * (p : ℝ) * (j : ℝ)) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / (p : ℝ))` when `a > 0` and
`p` is a positive natural number.
items.title: ofParabolicRecurrence

items.label: ofQuadraticRecurrence
items.statement:
A positive sequence tending to zero whose quadratic-recurrence residual
`ε (j + 1) - ε j + a * ε j ^ 2` is `O(ε j ^ 3)` is asymptotic to
the explicit reciprocal scale `(a * (j : ℝ))⁻¹`.
items.title: ofQuadraticRecurrence

items.label: ofQuarticRecurrence
items.statement:
A positive sequence tending to zero whose quartic-recurrence residual
`ε (j + 1) - ε j + a * ε j ^ 4` is `O(ε j ^ 5)` is asymptotic to
the parabolic scale `(3 * a * (j : ℝ)) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / 3)`.
items.title: ofQuarticRecurrence

items.title: of_even_odd

items.label: summable_rpow_iff
items.statement:
If `ε j` is asymptotic to `C * j ^ (-1 / p)` for positive `C` and `p`,
then the sequence `ε j ^ q` is summable exactly when `p < q`.
items.title: summable_rpow_iff

items.label: tail_rpow_isBigO
items.statement:
Under the same power-scale asymptotic hypotheses, the shifted `q`-power tail is
`O(j ^ (1 - q / p))` whenever `p < q`.
items.title: tail_rpow_isBigO

items.label: tail_rpow_isBigO_self
items.statement:
Under the same power-scale asymptotic hypotheses, the shifted `q`-power tail is
`O(ε j ^ (q - p))` whenever `p < q`.
items.title: tail_rpow_isBigO_self

items.label: tail_rpow_isEquivalent
items.statement:
If `ε j` is asymptotic to `C * j ^ (-1 / p)` for positive `C` and `p`, then
for `p < q` its shifted `q`-power tail has sharp asymptotic coefficient
`C ^ q * (p / (q - p))`.
items.title: tail_rpow_isEquivalent

items.label: tail_rpow_isEquivalent_self
items.statement:
If `ε j` is asymptotic to `C * j ^ (-1 / p)` for positive `C` and `p`, then
for `p < q` its shifted `q`-power tail is asymptotic to
`C ^ p * (p / (q - p)) * ε j ^ (q - p)`.
items.title: tail_rpow_isEquivalent_self

items.label: tsum_nat_add
items.statement:

items.title: tsum_nat_add

items.label: inner_apply_bounds_of_norm_le
items.statement:
A continuous linear endomorphism bounded in operator norm by `η` has quadratic form
between `-η * ‖v‖ ^ 2` and `η * ‖v‖ ^ 2`.
items.title: inner_apply_bounds_of_norm_le

items.label: isPositive_le_norm_smul_one
items.statement: A positive endomorphism is bounded above by its norm times the identity.
items.title: isPositive_le_norm_smul_one

items.label: isPositive_of_loewner_lowerBound
items.statement: A nonnegative Loewner lower bound makes a continuous self-endomorphism positive.
items.title: isPositive_of_loewner_lowerBound

items.label: isUnit_of_loewner_lowerBound
items.statement: A strict Loewner lower bound makes a continuous self-endomorphism invertible.

adjoint.

items.label: norm_le_of_selfAdjoint_loewner_abs_bound

A self-adjoint operator bounded in Loewner order by a scalar identity has the corresponding norm
bound.
items.title: norm_le_of_selfAdjoint_loewner_abs_bound

items.label: norm_pullback_le
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: adjoint congruence multiplies an
operator norm by at most the square of the coordinate map's norm.
This estimate is upstream-worthy for the Hessian coordinate-change API.
items.title: norm_pullback_le

items.label: norm_sq_adjoint_lower_bound

A lower Loewner bound on `L ∘ L†` gives the corresponding squared-norm lower bound
for the adjoint.
items.title: norm_sq_adjoint_lower_bound

items.title: positive_form_cauchySchwarz

items.statement:
If `x = O(α)` and a perturbation `y` is both `O(α)` and `O(β)`, then the
change of an `n`-homogeneous diagonal multilinear expression is
`O(α^(n-1) β)`.
items.title: diagonal_add_sub_isBigO

items.label: frame_col_one
items.statement: The second column of the frame is the positively oriented perpendicular direction.
items.title: frame_col_one

items.label: frame_col_zero

items.title: frame_col_zero

items.title: frame_mem_specialOrthogonalGroup

items.title: metric_posDef

items.label: ofParams_gradient
items.statement: The gradient of a state built by `ofParams` has the displayed frame-coordinate form.
items.title: ofParams_gradient

items.label: ofParams_metric
items.statement: The metric of a state built by `ofParams` has the displayed diagonal-frame form.
items.title: ofParams_metric

items.label: ofSpectral_amplitude

The amplitude projection of a spectrally recovered state is its low oriented gradient
coordinate.

items.label: ofSpectral_gradient
items.statement:
A spectrally recovered state has the prescribed positive oriented gradient coordinates in
its frame.
items.title: ofSpectral_gradient

items.label: ofSpectral_h
items.statement: The high-metric projection of a spectrally recovered state is its high spectral value.
items.title: ofSpectral_h

items.label: ofSpectral_metric
items.statement: A spectrally recovered state has the prescribed ordered spectrum in its oriented frame.
items.title: ofSpectral_metric

items.label: ofSpectral_p
items.statement: The shape projection of a spectrally recovered state is its recovery formula.
items.title: ofSpectral_p

items.label: ofSpectral_r
items.statement: The radius projection of a spectrally recovered state is its recovery formula.
items.title: ofSpectral_r

items.label: ofSpectral_spec
items.statement:
Spectral recovery produces positive canonical parameters with the prescribed projections,
metric spectrum, and oriented gradient coordinates.
items.title: ofSpectral_spec

items.label: perp_eq
items.statement: The perpendicular direction has the prescribed coordinate formula.
items.title: perp_eq

items.label: recoveryHigh_mul_shape_mul_radius_sq
items.statement:
The high spectral value times the recovered shape and squared radius is the low spectral
value.
items.title: recoveryHigh_mul_shape_mul_radius_sq

items.label: recoveryRadius_pos
items.statement:
The recovered radius is positive for positive ordered spectral values and positive oriented
gradient coordinates.
