The named metric triple is definitionally the triple used by the normal-form metric
analyticity theorem.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondMetricTriple_eq

items.label: independentRadiusSecondMetricTriple_zero

items.title: independentRadiusSecondMetricTriple_zero

items.statement: The normalized second-leg metric triple is analytic at each zero-radius base point.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondMetric_analyticAt

items.title: independentRadiusSecondMetric_zero

The normalized second-leg residual triple has its explicit
first derivative at zero.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondResiduals_hasDerivAt

items.title: independentRadiusSecondResiduals_zero

The normalized second-leg spectral pair has derivative
`(b (2 J + P - 12), 8 b)` at zero radius.

items.title: independentRadiusSecondSpectral_analyticAt

items.title: independentRadiusSecondSpectral_hasDerivAt

items.label: independentRadiusSecondSpectral_hasDerivAt_of_factorization
items.statement:
An explicit factorization with the corrected second-leg
spectral jet transports to `independentRadiusSecondSpectral`.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondSpectral_hasDerivAt_of_factorization

items.label: independentRadiusSecondSpectral_zero
items.statement: The second normalized spectral factors have base value `(2,1)`.
items.title: independentRadiusSecondSpectral_zero

items.label: independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_congr
items.statement: Exact pointwise equality preserves an independent-radius truncated germ.
items.title: independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_congr

items.label: independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_of_eventuallyEq
items.statement: An eventual equality of scalar families preserves an independent-radius truncated germ.
items.title: independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_of_eventuallyEq

items.label: independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_of_quadraticGerms
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the same quadratic certificates give the truncated
three-term germ whose compact-uniform remainder has order three.
items.title: independentRadiusTruncatedGerm_of_quadraticGerms

items.label: independentRawRecoveredTriple_eq_normalizedFactors_of_secondStep
items.statement:
After a concrete second raw step has been identified,
its frame-level recovery data determine the normalized independent-radius triple.
items.title: independentRawRecoveredTriple_eq_normalizedFactors_of_secondStep

items.label: independentRawRecoveredTriple_negate_gradient
items.statement:
When the output gradient is not orthogonal to the low
eigenvector, simultaneous sign changes in the input gradient leave raw recovery unchanged.
items.title: independentRawRecoveredTriple_negate_gradient

items.label: independentRawStep_first_eq
items.statement:
The first independent-radius raw step is the
normalized first-step metric and gradient once its secant-step side conditions
are supplied.
items.title: independentRawStep_first_eq

items.label: independentRawStep_metric_posDef
items.statement: A valid raw DFP step preserves positive definiteness of its metric component.
items.title: independentRawStep_metric_posDef

items.label: independentRawStep_negate_gradient
items.statement:
One DFP raw step is equivariant under negating its
incoming gradient; its updated matrix is unchanged and its updated gradient is negated.
items.title: independentRawStep_negate_gradient

items.label: independentRawStep_second_eq
items.statement:
The second independent-radius raw step is the
normalized second-step metric and gradient for a diagonal first-leg state.
items.title: independentRawStep_second_eq

items.label: independentSecondStep_spec
items.statement: The second independent-radius DFP step has the displayed normalized matrix and gradient.
items.title: independentSecondStep_spec

items.label: input_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the mixed canonical input.
items.title: input_apply

items.label: input_uncurry_contDiffAt
items.statement:
The canonical input map is `C^m` at every independent-radius base point for
Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale).
items.title: input_uncurry_contDiffAt

items.label: iteratedDeriv_two_of_secondDerivativeTransport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a second derivative of an abstract scalar
factor path transports through a pointwise identification of that path.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_two_of_secondDerivativeTransport

items.label: lowFrame_transpose_mulVec
items.statement:
The transpose of the fixed low-eigenvector frame gives the two explicit normalized
gradient coordinates of a planar vector.
items.title: lowFrame_transpose_mulVec

items.label: lowGradientChartPath_quadraticGerm_of_componentGerms
items.statement:
Supporting Lemma companion: component quadratic germs combine into the
canonical low-gradient quadratic germ.  The quadratic coefficient is
independent of the metric diagonal jets and equals `q₂ - c₁² / 2`.
items.title: lowGradientChartPath_quadraticGerm_of_componentGerms

items.label: low_eq_radiusSq_mul_detFactor
items.statement:
The physical low eigenvalue of a radius-scaled symmetric matrix is the squared radius
times its determinant factor whenever the high eigenvalue is nonzero.
items.title: low_eq_radiusSq_mul_detFactor

items.label: map_fixedScale
items.statement:
Away from zero signed scale and near the canonical base state, specializing the
independent radius to `ε ^ 2` agrees with the square of the signed-scale coordinate
of `DFP.TwoLeg.stateMap`.
items.title: map_fixedScale

items.label: map_zero
items.statement: The removable mixed map fixes the canonical base state for every control scale.
items.title: map_zero

items.label: mem_parameterSet
items.statement:
Membership in the mixed parameter set separates into the control interval and
the coefficient ball.
items.title: mem_parameterSet

items.label: mixedIndependentRadiusCancellation
items.statement:
The bounded-control independent-radius cancellation supplies the three local germs on
the strip `|b| < 1 / 4` for Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius,
shape, and scale).
items.title: mixedIndependentRadiusCancellation

items.label: mixedIndependentRadiusCoefficientGerms
items.statement:
The independent-radius two-leg map has the radius, shape, and scale coefficient germs
required by Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale).
items.title: mixedIndependentRadiusCoefficientGerms

items.label: mixedInput_zero
items.statement:
The mixed input at zero radius is the canonical base state for Supporting Lemma
(Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale).
items.title: mixedInput_zero

items.label: mixedMap_input_zero
items.statement:
The mixed map evaluated on its zero-radius input is the canonical base output for
Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale).
items.title: mixedMap_input_zero

items.label: mixedRadiusCoefficientGerm
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale), the
radius output has the stated factorial-normalized coefficients through order three.
items.title: mixedRadiusCoefficientGerm

items.label: mixedRadius_constantCoeff
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale), the
constant Taylor coefficient of the mixed radius output is zero.
items.title: mixedRadius_constantCoeff

items.label: mixedScaleCoefficientGerm
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale), the
recovered high scale has the stated factorial-normalized coefficients through order two.
items.title: mixedScaleCoefficientGerm

items.label: mixedScale_constantCoeff
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale), the
constant Taylor coefficient of the mixed high-scale output is one.
items.title: mixedScale_constantCoeff

items.label: mixedShapeCoefficientGerm
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale), the
recovered shape has the stated factorial-normalized coefficients through order two.
items.title: mixedShapeCoefficientGerm

items.label: mixedShape_constantCoeff
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale), the
constant Taylor coefficient of the mixed shape output is two.
items.title: mixedShape_constantCoeff

items.label: orientedEigenframe_eq_fixed_or_neg
items.statement: A gradient-oriented eigenframe is the fixed low-eigenvector frame up to one global sign.
items.title: orientedEigenframe_eq_fixed_or_neg

items.label: orientedEigenframe_frame_negate_gradient_of_inner_ne_zero
items.statement:
Away from the orthogonality boundary, negating the gradient
flips the oriented low-eigenvector frame by one global sign.
items.title: orientedEigenframe_frame_negate_gradient_of_inner_ne_zero

items.label: orientedRecoveryTriple_eq_normalizedFactors_of_frame
items.statement:
An oriented planar frame with the prescribed low/high
eigenvalue and gradient coordinates produces the normalized recovery triple, independently
of the global sign chosen by the orientation test.
items.title: orientedRecoveryTriple_eq_normalizedFactors_of_frame

items.label: orientedRecovery_eq_normalizedFactors
items.statement:
Recovery from an oriented planar eigenframe agrees with the normalized radius-factor
formulas when the physical low eigenvalue and second gradient coordinate carry radius factors.
items.title: orientedRecovery_eq_normalizedFactors

items.label: parameterSetControlAbsLt
items.statement: Membership in `parameterSet β B` bounds the signed control coordinate by `1 / 4`.
items.title: parameterSetControlAbsLt

items.label: parameterSet_isCompact
items.statement:
Independent-radius mixed expansion prerequisite: the bounded mixed parameter region is
compact whenever its radius parameters are finite.
items.title: parameterSet_isCompact

items.label: physicalAmplitudeQuadraticGerm_of_componentTransport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the physical amplitude inherits the quadratic
germ computed from four spectral/gradient component germs.
items.title: physicalAmplitudeQuadraticGerm_of_componentTransport

items.label: physicalAmplitudeRemainder_of_componentTransport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the component transport directly supplies the
explicit third-order amplitude remainder consumed by physical-drift estimates.
items.title: physicalAmplitudeRemainder_of_componentTransport

items.label: quadraticModel_deriv_at_zero
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the derivative of a quadratic model at the origin is
its linear coefficient.
items.title: quadraticModel_deriv_at_zero

items.label: quadraticModel_iteratedDeriv_two_at_zero
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the second iterated derivative of a quadratic model
at the origin is twice its quadratic coefficient.
items.title: quadraticModel_iteratedDeriv_two_at_zero

items.label: radiusCoefficient_polynomial
items.statement:
Independent-radius mixed expansion prerequisite: the radius coefficient polynomial is the
displayed constant, linear, and quadratic expression.
items.title: radiusCoefficient_polynomial

items.label: radiusExpansion
items.statement:
Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale) (1):
uniformly for bounded `(b, P, J)`, the independent-radius update has the stated
quadratic term and an order-three remainder.
items.title: radiusExpansion

items.label: radiusRemainderOn_of_directGerm
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale), a
direct radius coefficient germ gives the corresponding paper-facing remainder.
items.title: radiusRemainderOn_of_directGerm

items.label: radiusRemainderOn_of_germ
items.statement:
Independent-radius mixed expansion prerequisite: a radius coefficient germ supplies the
paper-facing order-three radius remainder for any positive coefficient.
items.title: radiusRemainderOn_of_germ

items.label: realSymmetric2_high_pos_of_posDef
items.statement: The upper eigenvalue of a positive-definite real symmetric planar matrix is positive.
items.title: realSymmetric2_high_pos_of_posDef

items.label: recoveryFactors_hasDerivAt_of_componentJets
items.statement:
Component derivative data at `(S 0, G 0) = ((2,1),(1,2))`
determine the first derivative of the recovered radius, shape, and high-scale factors.  The
squared denominator in the shape quotient contributes the coefficient `4 * g₁`.
items.title: recoveryFactors_hasDerivAt_of_componentJets

items.label: recoveryRadiusPathQuadraticGerm_of_componentGerms
items.statement:
Supporting fact: multiplying the recovered radius factor by the
independent radius shifts the same quadratic germ by one order.
items.title: recoveryRadiusPathQuadraticGerm_of_componentGerms

items.label: recoveryRadiusQuadraticGerm_of_componentGerms
items.statement:
Supporting fact: canonical spectral and gradient component germs
determine the recovered radius factor through quadratic order.
items.title: recoveryRadiusQuadraticGerm_of_componentGerms

items.label: recoveryRadius_neg_neg
items.statement:
Simultaneous negation of the two gradient coordinates
does not change the recovered radius quotient.
items.title: recoveryRadius_neg_neg

items.label: recoveryShape_neg_neg
items.statement:
Simultaneous negation of the two gradient coordinates
does not change the recovered shape quotient.
items.title: recoveryShape_neg_neg

items.label: recoveryTriple_neg_neg
items.statement:
A recovered triple is unchanged when both oriented
gradient coordinates are negated.
items.title: recoveryTriple_neg_neg

items.label: scalarCoefficientGerm_residual_eq
items.statement:
Independent-radius mixed expansion prerequisite: a coefficient germ identifies the
finite Taylor remainder with the explicit polynomial residual.
items.title: scalarCoefficientGerm_residual_eq

items.label: scalarFamily_eventuallyEq_of_uncurry_radius
items.statement:
Supporting fact: an uncurried eventual equality specializes to
an eventual equality on every fixed-parameter radius path.
items.title: scalarFamily_eventuallyEq_of_uncurry_radius

items.label: scaleCoefficient_polynomial
items.statement:
Independent-radius mixed expansion prerequisite: the scale coefficient polynomial is the
displayed constant and linear expression.
items.title: scaleCoefficient_polynomial

items.label: scaleExpansion
items.statement:
Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale) (3):
uniformly for bounded `(b, P, J)`, the recovered high scale has linear term
`8 * b * r` and an order-two remainder.
items.title: scaleExpansion

items.label: scaleRemainderOn_of_directGerm
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale), a
direct scale coefficient germ gives the corresponding paper-facing remainder.
items.title: scaleRemainderOn_of_directGerm

items.label: scaleRemainderOn_of_germ
items.statement:
Independent-radius mixed expansion prerequisite: a scale coefficient germ supplies the
paper-facing order-two high-scale remainder for any positive coefficient.
items.title: scaleRemainderOn_of_germ

items.label: shapeCoefficient_polynomial
items.statement:
Independent-radius mixed expansion prerequisite: the shape coefficient polynomial is the
displayed constant and linear expression.
items.title: shapeCoefficient_polynomial

items.label: shapeExpansion
items.statement:
Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale) (2):
uniformly for bounded `(b, P, J)`, the recovered shape has the stated linear term
and an order-two remainder.
items.title: shapeExpansion

items.label: shapeRemainderOn_of_directGerm
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale), a
direct shape coefficient germ gives the corresponding paper-facing remainder.
items.title: shapeRemainderOn_of_directGerm

items.label: shapeRemainderOn_of_germ
items.statement:
Independent-radius mixed expansion prerequisite: a shape coefficient germ supplies the
paper-facing order-two shape remainder for any positive coefficient.
items.title: shapeRemainderOn_of_germ

items.label: truncatedGerm_of_uncurryEq_secondGradientLow
items.statement:
Supporting Lemma: any scalar family with a certified uncurried equality to
the normalized second-gradient low coordinate inherits its exact amplitude
coefficient germ.
items.title: truncatedGerm_of_uncurryEq_secondGradientLow

items.label: truncatedTaylor_sum_decomposition
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale),
the full scalar Taylor sum splits into its lower coefficients and the top coefficient.
items.title: truncatedTaylor_sum_decomposition

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_independentRadiusGerm
items.statement:
Independent-radius mixed expansion prerequisite: a compactly uniform scalar coefficient
germ yields its explicit scalar remainder estimate.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_independentRadiusGerm

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_independentRadiusTruncatedGerm
items.statement:
For Supporting Lemma (Mixed-variable expansion of radius, shape, and scale),
a truncated coefficient germ yields some positive compact-uniform remainder constant.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_independentRadiusTruncatedGerm

items.label: slowCurveFirstStepRemainder
items.statement:
Along a path whose shape and high-eigenvalue coordinates agree with the
polynomial slow graph through order four, the first normalized step norm equals
`2 * ε ^ 2 + (112 / 5) * ε ^ 5 - (11 / 5) * ε ^ 6` up to `O(ε ^ 7)`.
items.title: slowCurveFirstStepRemainder

items.label: slowCurveSecondStepRemainder
items.statement:
Along a path whose shape and high-eigenvalue coordinates agree with the
polynomial slow graph through order four, the second normalized step norm equals
`ε ^ 2 + (114 / 5) * ε ^ 5 - (49 / 10) * ε ^ 6` up to `O(ε ^ 7)`.
items.title: slowCurveSecondStepRemainder

items.label: slowFinalGradient
items.statement:
Along the polynomial slow-graph path, the final normalized gradient norm has the displayed
order-six finite Taylor jet.
items.title: slowFinalGradient

items.label: slowFinalGradientRemainder
items.statement:
Along a path whose shape and high-eigenvalue coordinates agree with the
polynomial slow graph through order four, the final normalized gradient norm
equals `1 - (9 / 2) * ε ^ 4 + (116 / 5) * ε ^ 6` up to `O(ε ^ 7)`.
items.title: slowFinalGradientRemainder

items.label: slowFirstStep
items.statement:
Along the polynomial slow-graph path, the first normalized step norm has the displayed
order-six finite Taylor jet.
items.title: slowFirstStep

items.label: slowInitialGradient
items.statement:
Along the polynomial slow-graph path, the initial normalized gradient norm has the
displayed order-five finite Taylor jet.
items.title: slowInitialGradient

items.label: slowInitialGradientRemainder
items.statement:
Along a path whose shape coordinate agrees with the polynomial slow graph
through order four, the initial normalized gradient norm equals
`1 + 2 * ε ^ 4` up to `O(ε ^ 6)`.
items.title: slowInitialGradientRemainder

items.label: slowIntermediateGradient
items.statement:
Along the polynomial slow-graph path, the intermediate normalized gradient norm has the
displayed order-six finite Taylor jet.
items.title: slowIntermediateGradient

items.label: slowIntermediateGradientRemainder
items.statement:
Along a path whose shape coordinate agrees with the polynomial slow graph
through order four, the intermediate normalized gradient norm equals
`1 - 2 * ε ^ 3 - 2 * ε ^ 4 - (112 / 5) * ε ^ 6` up to `O(ε ^ 7)`.
items.title: slowIntermediateGradientRemainder

items.label: slowSecondStep
items.statement:
Along the polynomial slow-graph path, the second normalized step norm has the displayed
order-six finite Taylor jet.
items.title: slowSecondStep

items.label: uniformOn
items.statement:
The five normalized step- and gradient-norm projections have one common order-seven
uniform finite-jet family on every closed ball of graph coefficients.
items.title: uniformOn

items.label: adjacentEndpointDistanceUpper
items.statement:
Consecutive flattened endpoints of every sufficiently small orbit carried
by an invariant slow curve are at most a constant times the endpoint radius.
items.title: adjacentEndpointDistanceUpper

items.label: bumpCorrectionContDiffTwoAndZeroJets
items.statement:
An invariant slow curve admits a common small-scale threshold on which the
endpoint-bump correction is twice continuously differentiable and has zero
value, gradient, and Hessian on its limiting circle.
items.title: bumpCorrectionContDiffTwoAndZeroJets

items.label: bumpCorrectionExtension
items.statement:
The endpoint-bump correction along an invariant slow curve is globally twice
continuously differentiable, vanishes on its limiting circle, interpolates the prescribed
endpoint jets, and has Hessian norm bounded linearly by the initial scale.
items.title: bumpCorrectionExtension

items.label: bumpCorrectionHessianBound
items.statement:
The Hessian norm of the endpoint-bump correction along an invariant slow curve is
bounded globally by a constant times the initial scale, uniformly over sufficiently small
initial scales.
items.title: bumpCorrectionHessianBound

items.label: endpointArmijo
items.statement:
Every sufficiently small endpoint step of an invariant slow-curve orbit
satisfies the scalar Armijo condition with coefficient `1 / 4`.
items.title: endpointArmijo

items.label: endpointArmijo_of_lt_two_thirds
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the endpoint Armijo inequality inherits any coefficient
`c₁` in the open interval `(0, 2 / 3)` from the uniform phase estimate.
items.title: endpointArmijo_of_lt_two_thirds

items.label: endpointBumpNormalizedJetBounds
items.statement:
Along an invariant slow curve, endpoint-bump values and first derivatives,
normalized by distance to the limiting circle, and second derivatives satisfy
uniform bounds at their respective powers of the cycle scale.
items.title: endpointBumpNormalizedJetBounds

items.label: endpointBumpSecondOrderJetsVanish
items.statement:
The normalized value, normalized first derivative, and second derivative
of endpoint bumps along an invariant slow curve vanish uniformly and
simultaneously as their supports approach the limiting circle.
items.title: endpointBumpSecondOrderJetsVanish

items.label: endpointBumpUniformBounds
items.statement:
A common threshold and positive constants uniformly control the value,
first derivative, and second derivative of every endpoint bump on its support
along an invariant slow curve.
items.title: endpointBumpUniformBounds

items.label: endpointClusterPt_mem_limitCircle
items.statement:
Every cluster point of the endpoints of a sufficiently small invariant
slow-curve orbit belongs to its limiting circle.
items.title: endpointClusterPt_mem_limitCircle

items.label: interpolationBallsEventuallyNearLimitCircle
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small invariant slow curve, every positive closed
thickening of the limiting circle eventually contains every interpolation
ball.
items.title: interpolationBallsEventuallyNearLimitCircle

items.label: interpolationClosedBallDisjointLimitCircle
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small invariant slow curve, every closed
interpolation ball is disjoint from the limiting circle.
items.title: interpolationClosedBallDisjointLimitCircle

items.label: interpolationRadiusAndLimitCircleDistanceTendstoZero
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small invariant slow curve, interpolation radii and
endpoint distances to the limiting circle both tend to zero.
items.title: interpolationRadiusAndLimitCircleDistanceTendstoZero

items.label: interpolationRadiusTendstoZero
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small invariant slow curve, interpolation radii tend
to zero.
items.title: interpolationRadiusTendstoZero

items.label: interpolationRadiusUniformBounds
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small invariant slow curve, every interpolation
radius is bounded above and below by positive multiples of the corresponding
endpoint radius.
items.title: interpolationRadiusUniformBounds

items.label: interpolationRadius_isBigO_endpointRadius
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small invariant slow curve, interpolation radius is
big-O of endpoint radius.
items.title: interpolationRadius_isBigO_endpointRadius

items.label: interpolationRadius_pos
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small invariant slow curve, every interpolation
radius is strictly positive.
items.title: interpolationRadius_pos

items.label: ofAsymptotics_high
items.statement:
An invariant slow curve bundled by `ofAsymptotics` retains its high
coordinate.
items.title: ofAsymptotics_high

items.label: ofAsymptotics_shape
items.statement:
An invariant slow curve bundled by `ofAsymptotics` retains its shape
coordinate.
items.title: ofAsymptotics_shape

items.label: pairwiseDisjointInterpolationClosedBalls
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small invariant slow curve, the closed interpolation
balls form a pairwise-disjoint family.
items.title: pairwiseDisjointInterpolationClosedBalls

items.label: path_apply
items.statement: The invariant slow-curve path exposes its three coordinates.
items.title: path_apply

items.label: phaseCorrectionRatioUniformBound
items.statement:
Uniformly over both phases of an invariant slow curve, the endpoint
correction relative to predicted decrease is at most linear in the cycle
scale whenever the boundary centers converge.
items.title: phaseCorrectionRatioUniformBound

items.label: phaseDecreaseRatioLowerBound
items.statement:
A sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit has positive predicted
decrease and realized decrease ratio at least one half on both phases.
items.title: phaseDecreaseRatioLowerBound

items.label: phaseDecreaseRatioLowerBound_of_lt_two_thirds
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the realized decrease ratio approaches the two-phase
limit from below uniformly for every first Wolfe coefficient strictly below
`2 / 3`.
items.title: phaseDecreaseRatioLowerBound_of_lt_two_thirds

items.label: phasePredictedDecreaseUniformBounds
items.statement:
Uniformly over both phases of an invariant slow curve, predicted decrease
is bounded above and below by positive multiples of the squared endpoint
radius.
items.title: phasePredictedDecreaseUniformBounds

items.label: phaseStepNormUniformBounds
items.statement:
Uniformly over both phases of an invariant slow curve, every physical
step norm is bounded above and below by positive multiples of the endpoint
radius.
items.title: phaseStepNormUniformBounds

items.label: phaseStepRatioUniformBound
items.statement:
Uniformly over both phases of an invariant slow curve, the
squared-step-to-decrease ratio differs from the prescribed phase ratio by at
most a positive constant times the cycle scale.
items.title: phaseStepRatioUniformBound

items.label: realizedObjectiveHolderSharp
items.statement:
Helper for eq:counterexample-nonlipschitz: sufficiently small realizations
of an invariant slow curve have a globally one-half Hölder Hessian and no
larger Hölder exponent on any convex set containing their endpoints.
items.title: realizedObjectiveHolderSharp

items.label: scaleTendstoZero
items.statement:
The scale coordinate of every sufficiently small forward state-map orbit
carried by an invariant slow curve tends to zero.
items.title: scaleTendstoZero

items.label: stateMap_path_eventuallyEq
items.statement:
Applying the two-leg state map along an invariant slow curve eventually
agrees with reparametrization by the next scale.
items.title: stateMap_path_eventuallyEq

items.label: stateScaleTendstoZero
items.statement:
The physical state scale along every sufficiently small orbit carried by
an invariant slow curve tends to zero.
items.title: stateScaleTendstoZero

items.label: supportInfDistBoundsUniformInSupport
items.statement:
Below one slow-curve threshold, a single pair of comparison constants works
for every family supported in the interpolation balls of the same orbit.
items.title: supportInfDistBoundsUniformInSupport

items.label: supportInfDistLinearLower
items.statement:
Compatibility certificate combining the pure support-distance lower bound
with the scale interval and interpolation-radius positivity used by downstream
decay estimates.
items.title: supportInfDistLinearLower

items.label: supportInfDistLinearLowerBound
items.statement:
For a sufficiently small invariant slow curve, every family supported in
the interpolation balls stays at least a fixed positive multiple of the cycle
scale away from the limiting circle, uniformly over every index.
items.title: supportInfDistLinearLowerBound

items.label: supportInfDistUniformBounds
items.statement:
For any one family supported in the interpolation balls of a sufficiently
small invariant slow-curve orbit, distance from support points to the limiting
circle is eventually comparable to the current cycle scale.

This compatibility form follows from `supportInfDistBoundsUniformInSupport`,
whose constants are chosen before the support family.
items.title: supportInfDistUniformBounds

items.label: amplitudeRatio_sub_quartic_isBigO
items.statement:
On any fifth-order slow graph, the normalized amplitude ratio differs

items.label: weightedTransversePDefectJet
items.statement:
The shape-coordinate graph-invariance defect, evaluated at the updated signed
scale, has the displayed cubic and quartic coefficients.
items.title: weightedTransversePDefectJet

items.label: weightedTransversePDefectJet_via_scaleStationarity
items.statement:
The shape graph-invariance defect jet, with its scalar and mixed expansions
discharged by scale stationarity.
items.title: weightedTransversePDefectJet_via_scaleStationarity

items.label: weightedTransversePJet
items.statement:
Along a polynomial graph with arbitrary cubic and quartic coefficients,
the updated shape coordinate has the displayed order-four finite Taylor jet.
items.title: weightedTransversePJet

items.label: weightedTransversePJet_of_scale
items.statement: Assemble the recovered-shape jet once its pure scale-axis jet is known.
items.title: weightedTransversePJet_of_scale

items.label: weightedTransversePJet_of_scale_and_basis_cross
items.statement:
Basis-direction version of `weightedTransversePJet_of_scale_and_cross`.
The two Hessian assumptions are independent of the graph coefficients.
items.title: weightedTransversePJet_of_scale_and_basis_cross

items.label: weightedTransversePJet_of_scale_and_cross
items.statement:
The weighted transverse-shape jet follows from the scale-axis jet once the
single quadratic scale/transverse cross derivative is known to vanish.
items.title: weightedTransversePJet_of_scale_and_cross

items.label: weightedTransversePJet_of_scale_and_mixed
items.statement:
Assemble the weighted transverse-shape jet from its scale-axis jet and an
order-five mixed-interaction estimate.
items.title: weightedTransversePJet_of_scale_and_mixed

items.label: weightedTransversePJet_via_scaleStationarity
items.statement: Full weighted shape jet, with every mixed Hessian discharged by scale stationarity.
items.title: weightedTransversePJet_via_scaleStationarity

items.label: weightedTransverseRemainder
items.statement:
On every closed ball of graph coefficients with nonnegative radius, both
transverse graph-invariance defects have one joint uniform remainder of order five.
items.title: weightedTransverseRemainder

items.label: weightedZeroScaleNormalizedRadiusJet
items.statement:
The zero-scale radius jet contains exactly the part of the weighted radius coefficients that
depends on the cubic and quartic transverse graph coefficients.
items.title: weightedZeroScaleNormalizedRadiusJet

items.label: weightedZeroScaleTransverseHJet
items.statement:
The zero-scale updated-high-coordinate jet is constant through order four, independently of
the cubic and quartic transverse graph coefficients.
items.title: weightedZeroScaleTransverseHJet

items.label: weightedZeroScaleTransversePJet
items.statement:
The zero-scale updated-shape jet contains exactly the coefficient-dependent part of the
weighted transverse shape jet.
items.title: weightedZeroScaleTransversePJet

items.statement:

oriented-angle error is bounded cubically in that radius.

items.label: bumpCorrection_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the global bump correction as a pointwise finsum.
items.title: bumpCorrection_apply

items.label: bumpCorrection_endpoint
items.statement:
The disjoint endpoint-bump correction vanishes at every endpoint when the interpolation
radii are positive and the interpolation balls are pairwise disjoint.
items.title: bumpCorrection_endpoint

items.label: bumpCorrection_eq_finsum_scaledLinearBump
items.statement:
The global bump correction is the pointwise finsum of the corresponding
generic scaled linear bumps.
items.title: bumpCorrection_eq_finsum_scaledLinearBump

items.label: bumpCorrection_eq_tsum
items.statement: The finsum-defined endpoint correction equals the pointwise endpoint-bump tsum.
items.title: bumpCorrection_eq_tsum

items.label: bumpCorrection_gradient_endpoint
items.statement:
The canonical gradient of the endpoint-bump correction at an endpoint is its prescribed
endpoint correction vector.
items.title: bumpCorrection_gradient_endpoint

items.label: bumpCorrection_hasGradientAt_endpoint
items.statement: The endpoint-bump correction has the prescribed endpoint correction as its Fréchet gradient.
items.title: bumpCorrection_hasGradientAt_endpoint

items.label: bumpCorrection_hessian_endpoint
items.statement:
Helper for eq:endpoint-data: disjoint interpolation bumps have zero Hessian
at every interpolation center, since their cutoff is locally constant there.
items.title: bumpCorrection_hessian_endpoint

items.label: closedSetCandidate_eq
items.statement:
The endpoint closed-set candidate is the union of its limiting circle and
the range of the flattened endpoint sequence.
items.title: closedSetCandidate_eq

items.label: contDiff_endpointBump
items.statement:
Every endpoint bump is infinitely continuously differentiable, independently
of the endpoint data and interpolation radius.
items.title: contDiff_endpointBump

items.label: cycleCountBound_of_twoPhaseGap
items.statement:
An antitone two-phase angle lift with quadratic phase-gap bounds controls the
angular displacement across a positive number of cycles.  The factor `10` accounts
for the two phase gaps in a cycle and the two possible endpoint phases.
items.title: cycleCountBound_of_twoPhaseGap

items.label: endpointBump_activeIndices_subsingleton
items.statement: At each point, at most one endpoint bump has a nonzero value.
items.title: endpointBump_activeIndices_subsingleton

items.label: endpointBump_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the cutoff bump attached to an endpoint.
items.title: endpointBump_apply

items.label: endpointBump_eq_scaledLinearBump
items.statement: The endpoint bump is the generic scaled linear bump specialized to the endpoint data.
items.title: endpointBump_eq_scaledLinearBump

items.label: endpointBump_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport
items.statement: Pairwise-disjoint interpolation balls give pairwise-disjoint endpoint-bump supports.
items.title: endpointBump_pairwiseDisjoint_tsupport

items.label: endpointBump_summable
items.statement: At each point, the endpoint-bump family is summable.
items.title: endpointBump_summable

items.label: endpointBump_tsum_eq_of_ne_zero
items.statement: If endpoint bump `k` is nonzero at a point, the pointwise tsum is that bump.
items.title: endpointBump_tsum_eq_of_ne_zero

items.label: endpointBump_tsupport_subset_interpolationClosedBall
items.statement: The topological support of an endpoint bump lies in its interpolation closed ball.
items.title: endpointBump_tsupport_subset_interpolationClosedBall

items.label: endpointCenter_def

items.title: endpointCenter_def

items.title: endpointCenter_even

items.label: endpointCenter_odd
items.statement: At an odd endpoint, `endpointCenter` is the corresponding intermediate center.
items.title: endpointCenter_odd

items.label: endpointCorrection_def
items.statement:
The endpoint correction is the prescribed gradient minus the translated
endpoint.
items.title: endpointCorrection_def

items.statement: The endpoint correction is the limiting center minus the endpoint center.
items.title: endpointCorrection_eq_center

items.label: endpointCorrection_even
items.statement: At an even endpoint, the correction is the limiting center minus the boundary center.
items.title: endpointCorrection_even

items.label: endpointCorrection_odd
items.statement: At an odd endpoint, the correction is the limiting center minus the intermediate center.
items.title: endpointCorrection_odd

items.label: endpointCurvatureCertificates
items.statement:
Every flattened physical endpoint step of an exact two-phase orbit
satisfies weak curvature with `c₂ = 3 / 4` and has positive secant curvature.
items.title: endpointCurvatureCertificates

items.label: endpointCurvatureCertificates_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the endpoint strong/weak curvature certificates are
available together for every `c₂ ≥ 2 / 3`.
items.title: endpointCurvatureCertificates_of_ge_two_thirds

items.label: endpointGradientAngleLift_coe
items.statement: Coercing an endpoint-gradient lift recovers its quotient-valued direction angle.
items.title: endpointGradientAngleLift_coe

items.label: endpointGradientAngleLift_succ
items.statement: The endpoint-gradient lift advances by the canonical representative of the next angle gap.
items.title: endpointGradientAngleLift_succ

items.label: endpointGradientAngleLift_succ_sub
items.statement:
Consecutive endpoint-gradient lifts differ by the canonical representative of their
quotient-angle gap.
items.title: endpointGradientAngleLift_succ_sub

items.label: endpointGradientAngleLift_zero
items.statement: The endpoint-gradient lift starts at the canonical representative of the zeroth angle.
items.title: endpointGradientAngleLift_zero

items.label: endpointGradientAngle_def
items.statement: The endpoint-gradient angle is measured from the first standard basis vector.
items.title: endpointGradientAngle_def

items.label: endpointGradientAngle_nextEven_sub_odd
items.statement:
Within an exact cycle, the gradient angle from its odd endpoint to the next even
endpoint is the second normalized endpoint-angle observable.
items.title: endpointGradientAngle_nextEven_sub_odd

items.label: endpointGradientAngle_odd_sub_even
items.statement:
Within an exact cycle, the gradient angle from the even endpoint to the following
odd endpoint is the first normalized endpoint-angle observable.
items.title: endpointGradientAngle_odd_sub_even

items.label: endpointGradientNorm_mem_Icc_of_amplitude_and_normalized
items.statement:
Amplitude and normalized-observable intervals give a uniform endpoint-gradient interval,
with the even and odd endpoint branches transported separately.
items.title: endpointGradientNorm_mem_Icc_of_amplitude_and_normalized

items.label: endpointGradient_eq_exactStepTransport
items.statement:
Exact-cycle data transports the flattened endpoint gradient directly from
the selected abstract step.
items.title: endpointGradient_eq_exactStepTransport

items.label: endpointGradient_eq_phaseGradient
items.statement: The flattened endpoint gradient is the physical gradient of the selected phase.
items.title: endpointGradient_eq_phaseGradient

items.label: endpointGradient_even
items.statement:
At an even endpoint, `endpointGradient` is the corresponding cycle-boundary
gradient.
items.title: endpointGradient_even

items.label: endpointGradient_odd
items.statement:
At an odd endpoint, `endpointGradient` is the corresponding intermediate
first-leg gradient.
items.title: endpointGradient_odd

items.label: endpointGradient_succ_eq_exactStepTransport
items.statement:
The flattened endpoint gradient after an exact phase is the next abstract
gradient transported by that phase's frame.
items.title: endpointGradient_succ_eq_exactStepTransport

items.label: endpointMetric_eq_exactStepTransport
items.statement:
Exact-cycle data transports the flattened metric directly from the
selected abstract step.
items.title: endpointMetric_eq_exactStepTransport

items.label: endpointMetric_eq_phaseMetric
items.statement:
The flattened endpoint metric at a structured phase index is the physical
metric selected for that phase.
items.title: endpointMetric_eq_phaseMetric

items.label: endpointMetric_even
items.statement: At an even endpoint, `endpointMetric` is the corresponding cycle-boundary metric.
items.title: endpointMetric_even

items.label: endpointMetric_odd
items.statement: At an odd endpoint, `endpointMetric` is the corresponding intermediate metric.
items.title: endpointMetric_odd

items.label: endpointMetric_posDef
items.statement:
Every inverse-Hessian matrix in the flattened sequence of an exact
two-phase orbit is positive definite.
items.title: endpointMetric_posDef

items.label: endpointMetric_succ_eq_exactStepTransport
items.statement:
The flattened metric after an exact phase is the transported next inverse
Hessian of the selected abstract step.
items.title: endpointMetric_succ_eq_exactStepTransport

items.label: endpointPhaseSlope_transport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the two physical endpoint pairings of a
phase are the slope and next-slope of its abstract secant step.
items.title: endpointPhaseSlope_transport

items.label: endpointPhaseStrongCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: every exact phase has strong-Wolfe curvature for any
`c₂` with `2 / 3 ≤ c₂`, using the exact phase ratios.
items.title: endpointPhaseStrongCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds

items.label: endpointPhaseWeakCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: every exact phase has weak-Wolfe curvature for any
`c₂` in the paper's range, again using the exact phase ratios.
items.title: endpointPhaseWeakCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds

items.label: endpointPolarAngleLift_coe
items.statement: Coercing an unwrapped endpoint polar angle recovers its quotient-valued angle.
items.title: endpointPolarAngleLift_coe

items.label: endpointPolarAngleLift_succ
items.statement: The endpoint polar-angle lift advances by the canonical representative of the next angle gap.
items.title: endpointPolarAngleLift_succ

items.label: endpointPolarAngleLift_succ_sub
items.statement:
Consecutive lifted values differ by the canonical real representative of the
quotient-angle gap.
items.title: endpointPolarAngleLift_succ_sub

In the local signed-angle interval, the recursive increment is the unique representative
of the corresponding quotient-valued endpoint-angle gap.

items.label: endpointPolarAngleLift_zero
items.statement: The endpoint polar-angle lift starts at the canonical representative of the zeroth angle.
items.title: endpointPolarAngleLift_zero

items.label: endpointPolarAngle_def
items.statement: The endpoint polar angle is the oriented angle from the first standard basis vector.

items.label: endpointPolarAngle_even
items.statement: The polar angle at an even index is the angle of the corresponding boundary endpoint.

items.statement: A nonzero endpoint displacement is reconstructed from its norm and polar angle.
items.title: endpointPolarAngle_spec

items.statement:
The quotient-valued endpoint polar angle minus the gradient angle is the physical
oriented angle from the endpoint gradient to the radial displacement.
items.title: endpointPolarAngle_sub_gradientAngle

items.label: endpointPredictedDecrease_eq_exactStep
items.statement:
The physical predicted decrease between adjacent flattened endpoints is the
predicted decrease of the selected abstract step.
items.title: endpointPredictedDecrease_eq_exactStep

items.label: endpointRadius_def
items.statement: The endpoint radius is the square of its cycle scale.
items.title: endpointRadius_def

items.label: endpointRadius_even
items.statement: At an even endpoint, the radius is the square of the corresponding cycle scale.
items.title: endpointRadius_even

items.label: endpointRadius_odd
items.statement: At an odd endpoint, the radius is the square of the corresponding cycle scale.
items.title: endpointRadius_odd

items.label: endpointScale_mul_radius
items.statement: The cube of an endpoint's cycle scale is that scale times its endpoint radius.
items.title: endpointScale_mul_radius

items.label: endpointSecantCurvature_pos
items.statement:
Every flattened endpoint step of an exact two-phase orbit has positive
gradient-displacement secant curvature.
items.title: endpointSecantCurvature_pos

items.label: endpointStepLength_eq_exactStep
items.statement:
The flattened exact step length at a structured phase index is the step
length of the selected abstract secant step.
items.title: endpointStepLength_eq_exactStep

items.label: endpointStepLength_even
items.statement: At an even endpoint, `endpointStepLength` is the first exact phase's step length.
items.title: endpointStepLength_even

items.label: endpointStepLength_odd
items.statement: At an odd endpoint, `endpointStepLength` is the second exact phase's step length.
items.title: endpointStepLength_odd

items.label: endpointStepNorm_eq_exactStep
items.statement:
The adjacent flattened-endpoint distance has the norm of the selected
abstract displacement.
items.title: endpointStepNorm_eq_exactStep

items.label: endpointStep_eq_exactStepTransport
items.statement:
Exact-cycle data transports the flattened adjacent-endpoint displacement
directly from the selected abstract step.
items.title: endpointStep_eq_exactStepTransport

items.label: endpointStep_eq_phaseDisplacement
items.statement:
The flattened adjacent-endpoint displacement is the physical displacement
of the selected phase.
items.title: endpointStep_eq_phaseDisplacement

items.label: endpointStrongCurvature
items.statement:
Every flattened endpoint step of an exact two-phase orbit has
strong curvature for any `c₂ ≥ 2 / 3`.
items.title: endpointStrongCurvature

items.label: endpointStrongCurvature_inequality_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the flattened strong-curvature theorem in
the absolute-inequality form consumed by gradient-facing strong-Wolfe APIs.
items.title: endpointStrongCurvature_inequality_of_ge_two_thirds

items.label: endpointStrongCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: every flattened exact-cycle endpoint has strong-Wolfe
curvature for all coefficients `c₂ ≥ 2 / 3`.
items.title: endpointStrongCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds

items.label: endpointStrongWolfe_of_endpointData
items.statement:
Endpoint gradient data and the exact two-phase ratio certificate
construct the strong-Wolfe predicate for every flattened endpoint step.
items.title: endpointStrongWolfe_of_endpointData

items.label: endpointWeakCurvature
items.statement:
Every flattened endpoint step of an exact two-phase orbit satisfies the
weak-Wolfe curvature condition with `c₂ = 3 / 4`.
items.title: endpointWeakCurvature

items.label: endpointWeakCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: every flattened exact-cycle endpoint has weak-Wolfe
curvature for all coefficients `c₂ ≥ 2 / 3`.
items.title: endpointWeakCurvature_of_ge_two_thirds

items.label: endpointWeakWolfe_of_endpointData
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: an endpoint Armijo inequality together with the
parameterized exact-cycle curvature certificate constructs the gradient-facing
weak-Wolfe predicate used by downstream iteration consumers.
items.title: endpointWeakWolfe_of_endpointData

items.label: endpoint_even
items.statement: The even flattened endpoint is the corresponding cycle-boundary point.
items.title: endpoint_even

items.label: endpoint_odd
items.statement: The odd flattened endpoint is the corresponding middle point.
items.title: endpoint_odd

items.label: evenSecantResidualNorm
items.statement:
Helper for eq:counterexample-nonlipschitz: the physical even-step secant
residual has norm exactly `εⱼ` times the physical step norm.
items.title: evenSecantResidualNorm

items.label: frameAngleIncrement_eq_observable
items.statement:
Each recursive frame-angle difference is the frame-angle field of the complete
observable map at the current normalized state.
items.title: frameAngleIncrement_eq_observable

items.label: frameAngleRepresentsLowVector
items.statement:
If an orbit starts in the identity frame and all relative updates remain in the
signed-angle chart, its accumulated angle rotates the initial low vector to the
current physical low vector.
items.title: frameAngleRepresentsLowVector

items.label: frameAngle_succ
items.statement: The accumulated frame angle advances by the current relative-frame angle.
items.title: frameAngle_succ

items.label: frameAngle_zero
items.statement: The accumulated frame angle starts at zero.
items.title: frameAngle_zero

items.label: gradientNorm_eq_amplitude_mul_initialObservable
items.statement: A valid boundary gradient factors into its positive amplitude and initial observable norm.
items.title: gradientNorm_eq_amplitude_mul_initialObservable

items.label: infDist_limitCircle
items.statement: The distance to an affine unit-sphere limiting circle is its absolute radial deviation.
items.title: infDist_limitCircle

items.label: inner_toLp_mulVec_eq_of_specialOrthogonal
items.statement:
Supporting fact: special-orthogonal phase transport preserves
the Euclidean pairings used by the endpoint Wolfe certificates.
items.title: inner_toLp_mulVec_eq_of_specialOrthogonal

items.label: interpolationClosedBall_disjoint_limitCircle
items.statement:
A positive endpoint isolation distance makes its interpolation ball
disjoint from the limiting circle, provided the endpoint is not on that
circle.
items.title: interpolationClosedBall_disjoint_limitCircle

items.label: interpolationRadius_def
items.statement:
The interpolation radius is one quarter of the infimum distance to the punctured
endpoint set.
items.title: interpolationRadius_def

items.label: interpolationRadius_eq_isolationDistance_div
items.statement:
The interpolation radius is one quarter of the endpoint isolation
distance.
items.title: interpolationRadius_eq_isolationDistance_div

items.label: interpolationRadius_eq_isolationRadius
items.statement:
The endpoint interpolation radius is the generic metric isolation radius in
the endpoint closed-set candidate.
items.title: interpolationRadius_eq_isolationRadius

items.label: interpolationRadius_lt_isolationDistance
items.statement:
A positive endpoint isolation distance strictly exceeds its interpolation
radius.
items.title: interpolationRadius_lt_isolationDistance

items.label: interpolationRadius_nonneg
items.statement: Endpoint interpolation radii are nonnegative.
items.title: interpolationRadius_nonneg

items.label: isClosed_closedSetCandidate
items.statement:
The endpoint candidate is closed when all endpoint cluster points lie on its
limiting circle.
items.title: isClosed_closedSetCandidate

items.label: isClosed_limitCircle
items.statement: A limiting circle with positive scale is closed.
items.title: isClosed_limitCircle

items.label: isCompact_limitCircle
items.statement: A positive-scale limiting circle is compact.
items.title: isCompact_limitCircle

items.label: isOrbit_of_exactCycles
items.statement:
Exactness of every two-phase cycle, together with gradient certificates
for an objective at the flattened endpoints, makes the flattened data a
classical inverse-form DFP orbit.
items.title: isOrbit_of_exactCycles

items.label: isolationDistance_def
items.statement: The endpoint isolation distance is the infimum distance to the punctured endpoint set.
items.title: isolationDistance_def

items.label: isolationDistance_nonneg
items.statement: Endpoint isolation distance is nonnegative.
items.title: isolationDistance_nonneg

items.label: iterateState_succ
items.statement: Iteration by the physical transition agrees with one further transition at a successor.
items.title: iterateState_succ

items.label: limitCircle_eq_sphere
items.statement: A limiting circle with positive scale is the corresponding metric sphere.
items.title: limitCircle_eq_sphere

items.label: limitCircle_nonempty
items.statement: A positive-scale limiting circle is nonempty.
items.title: limitCircle_nonempty

items.label: mapClusterPt_eq_of_tendsto
items.statement:
A cluster point of a sequence agrees with the sequence limit whenever the latter exists.

This is the basic `EndpointClusterSet/Basic` transport used to identify scalar limits
obtained from radial or angular error estimates.
items.title: mapClusterPt_eq_of_tendsto

items.label: mapClusterPt_mem_of_tendsto_infDist
items.statement:
A closed nonempty target contains every cluster point whose sequence distance to that
target tends to zero.

This is the metric `EndpointClusterSet/Basic` adapter for converting a radial remainder
estimate into a genuine cluster-set inclusion.
items.title: mapClusterPt_mem_of_tendsto_infDist

items.label: mapClusterSet_subset_limitCircle_of_tendsto_infDist
items.statement:
Every cluster point of an endpoint sequence belongs to a positive-scale limiting circle
when the endpoint distance to that circle tends to zero.

This is the one-sided `EndpointClusterSet/Basic` bridge; equality with the whole circle still
requires a separate angular recurrence or density hypothesis.
items.title: mapClusterSet_subset_limitCircle_of_tendsto_infDist

items.label: mem_closedSetCandidate
items.statement: Membership in the endpoint closed-set candidate.
items.title: mem_closedSetCandidate

items.label: mem_limitCircle
items.statement: Membership in the limiting circle in its affine unit-vector form.
items.title: mem_limitCircle

items.label: middleGradientNorm_eq_amplitude_mul_intermediateObservable
items.statement:
A valid intermediate gradient factors into its positive amplitude and
intermediate observable norm.
items.title: middleGradientNorm_eq_amplitude_mul_intermediateObservable

items.label: ofSlowCurveExact
items.statement:
For every sufficiently small positive initial scale, every physical cycle has valid
oriented phase data and agrees exactly with both abstract inverse-form DFP steps.
items.title: ofSlowCurveExact

items.label: ofSlowCurve_coordinates
items.statement:
The coordinates of the physical slow-curve orbit are the iterates of the signed
two-leg state map.
items.title: ofSlowCurve_coordinates

items.label: ofSlowCurve_phaseValidity
items.statement: Every sufficiently small slow-curve orbit has valid phase data at every cycle.
items.title: ofSlowCurve_phaseValidity

items.label: ofSlowCurve_succ
items.statement: Every slow-curve orbit applies the complete physical transition at the successor index.
items.title: ofSlowCurve_succ

items.label: ofSlowCurve_zero
items.statement: The slow-curve orbit starts at the explicit canonical physical state.
items.title: ofSlowCurve_zero

items.label: ofState_succ
items.statement: Every iterated orbit applies the complete physical transition at the successor index.
items.title: ofState_succ

items.label: ofState_zero
items.statement: An iterated orbit starts at its prescribed physical state.
items.title: ofState_zero

items.label: pairwiseDisjoint_interpolationClosedBall
items.statement:
Injectivity of the endpoint sequence makes its closed interpolation balls
pairwise disjoint.
items.title: pairwiseDisjoint_interpolationClosedBall

items.label: polarGradientLiftDifference_coe
items.statement:
Coercing the difference of the endpoint polar and gradient lifts gives the physical
polar-to-gradient correction angle.
items.title: polarGradientLiftDifference_coe

items.label: polarGradientLiftDifference_eq_correction_of_small
items.statement:
Small consecutive polar and gradient increments select a single real branch on
which the difference of their lifts equals the physical correction angle at every
endpoint.
items.title: polarGradientLiftDifference_eq_correction_of_small

items.label: polarGradientLiftDifference_zero_of_small
items.statement:
If the initial endpoint polar and gradient representatives are both in a common
quarter-turn chart, their lifted difference is the principal representative of the
physical correction angle.
items.title: polarGradientLiftDifference_zero_of_small

items.label: realizedObjective_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the realized objective at a point.
items.title: realizedObjective_apply

items.label: realizedObjective_decreaseRatio
items.statement:
The normalized decrease of the realized objective along an endpoint step is
the translated quadratic contribution plus the endpoint-correction contribution.
items.title: realizedObjective_decreaseRatio

items.label: realizedObjective_endpoint
items.statement:
The realized objective agrees with its translated quadratic part at every
interpolation endpoint.
items.title: realizedObjective_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_gradientChanges
items.statement:
The successive realized gradients along the endpoints have the same changes as
the prescribed abstract endpoint gradients.
items.title: realizedObjective_gradientChanges

items.label: realizedObjective_gradient_endpoint
items.statement:
At every interpolation endpoint, the realized objective has the prescribed
abstract endpoint gradient.
items.title: realizedObjective_gradient_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_gradient_formula_endpoint
items.statement:
At every interpolation endpoint, the gradient of the realized objective is the
translated quadratic gradient plus the endpoint correction.
items.title: realizedObjective_gradient_formula_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_hasEndpointGradientAt
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the endpoint gradient certificate of the
realized objective can be expressed with the orbit's prescribed gradient.
items.title: realizedObjective_hasEndpointGradientAt

items.label: realizedObjective_hasGradientAt_endpoint
items.statement:
The realized objective has the translated quadratic gradient plus the prescribed
endpoint correction at every interpolation endpoint.
items.title: realizedObjective_hasGradientAt_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_hessian_endpoint
items.statement:
Helper for eq:endpoint-data: the Hessian of the realized objective at an
interpolation endpoint is exactly the identity operator.
items.title: realizedObjective_hessian_endpoint

items.label: realizedObjective_isOrbit
items.statement:
The realized objective, prescribed endpoint step lengths, endpoints,
gradients, and inverse Hessians of an exact two-phase orbit satisfy the
classical inverse-form DFP recurrence.
items.title: realizedObjective_isOrbit

items.label: realizedObjective_not_hessianHolderOn
items.statement:
Helper for eq:counterexample-nonlipschitz: the concrete realized objective
cannot have a Hölder Hessian of exponent greater than one half on a convex
set containing its endpoints, whenever the physical steps are bounded by
a constant times the squares of the vanishing orbit scales.
items.title: realizedObjective_not_hessianHolderOn

items.label: slowCurveAdjacentEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Consecutive slow-curve endpoints have a uniform separation proportional to the
square of the scale of the cycle containing the earlier endpoint.
items.title: slowCurveAdjacentEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeAsymptotics
items.statement:
Every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit has a positive limiting
amplitude whose excess has first-order coefficient `13 / 3` in the scale.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeAsymptotics

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeDriftModulus
items.statement:
The canonical tail-supremum modulus uniformly controls the fourth-order
physical amplitude drift along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeDriftModulus

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeExistsPositiveLimit
items.statement:
For every sufficiently small positive initial scale, the amplitude of the canonical
slow-curve orbit converges to a strictly positive limit.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeExistsPositiveLimit

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeTailEquivalent
items.statement:
The amplitude excess of a sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit is
asymptotic to `(13 / 3) * Glim * ε` at every positive limiting amplitude `Glim`.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeTailEquivalent

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeTailUniform
items.statement:
A common right-hand modulus controls the first-order amplitude-tail error on every
sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeTailUniform

items.label: slowCurveAmplitudeUniformBounds
items.statement:
A common positive interval contains every amplitude and its limit on each sufficiently
small invariant slow-curve orbit with the prescribed jets.
items.title: slowCurveAmplitudeUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurveAngularGapEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Comparable slow-curve endpoints with a definite principal angular gap have a
uniform separation proportional to the square of the earlier endpoint scale.
items.title: slowCurveAngularGapEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowCurveArmijo
items.statement: The Armijo estimate for every endpoint step of an unbundled slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveArmijo

items.label: slowCurveBoundaryCenterTailIsBigO
items.statement:
For sufficiently small exact slow-curve orbits, cycle-boundary centers
approach any given limiting center with cubic order in the cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveBoundaryCenterTailIsBigO

items.label: slowCurveCenterIncrementNormSummable
items.statement:
The norms of the full-cycle center increments are summable on a sufficiently
small positive invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveCenterIncrementNormSummable

items.label: slowCurveCenterTailUniformBound
items.statement:
A single positive constant uniformly controls the boundary and intermediate
center tails of every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveCenterTailUniformBound

items.label: slowCurveCenterTendsto
items.statement:
The cycle-boundary centers of a sufficiently small positive invariant
slow-curve orbit converge in the Euclidean plane.
items.title: slowCurveCenterTendsto

items.label: slowCurveComparableScaleAmplitudeLoss
items.statement:
A comparable-scale interval of a positive slow-curve orbit has a uniform
positive fourth-order loss in physical amplitude at each intervening cycle.
items.title: slowCurveComparableScaleAmplitudeLoss

items.label: slowCurveDifferentScaleEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Chronologically ordered endpoints on sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbits
with a fixed scale gap are separated in endpoint distance at squared-scale order.
items.title: slowCurveDifferentScaleEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowCurveDifferentScaleRadialGap
items.statement:
Chronologically ordered endpoints on sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbits
with a fixed scale gap have a uniform first-order radial separation.
items.title: slowCurveDifferentScaleRadialGap

items.label: slowCurveEndpointAngleRemainderModulus
items.statement:
The canonical tail-supremum modulus uniformly controls both real endpoint-gradient
angle remainders along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointAngleRemainderModulus

items.label: slowCurveEndpointClusterSet_eq_limitCircle
items.statement:
The endpoint cluster set of a sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit
is the affine unit circle determined by its limiting center and amplitude.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointClusterSet_eq_limitCircle

items.label: slowCurveEndpointCorrectionRadiusUniformBound
items.statement: A single positive constant uniformly controls endpoint corrections by scale times endpoint radius.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointCorrectionRadiusUniformBound

items.label: slowCurveEndpointCorrectionUniformBound
items.statement: A single positive constant uniformly controls endpoint corrections by the cube of their cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointCorrectionUniformBound

items.label: slowCurveEndpointGradientNormTendsto
items.statement:
For every sufficiently small canonical slow-curve orbit, the norms of the
gradients along the full endpoint sequence converge to a strictly positive limit.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointGradientNormTendsto

items.label: slowCurveEndpointGradientNormUniformBounds
items.statement:
One common positive interval contains every endpoint-gradient norm on all
sufficiently small canonical slow-curve orbits.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointGradientNormUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurveEndpointLimitCircleDistanceEquivalent
items.statement:
The distance of every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve endpoint to
its limiting circle is asymptotic to the first-order amplitude excess.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointLimitCircleDistanceEquivalent

items.label: slowCurveEndpointLimitCircleInfDistUniformLower
items.statement:
Every endpoint of a sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit stays at
least a uniform positive multiple of its squared cycle scale from the limiting circle.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointLimitCircleInfDistUniformLower

items.label: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapExplicitBounds
items.statement:
Explicit-constant endpoint-angle gap bound: the two consecutive endpoint-angle
gaps lie between one half and five halves of the squared cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapExplicitBounds

items.label: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapLowerBound
items.statement:
Every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit has a consecutive lifted
endpoint-angle gap at least half the square of its cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapLowerBound

items.label: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapUniformBounds
items.statement:
For a sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the lifted physical endpoint
angles are strictly decreasing and each consecutive gap is uniformly comparable to
the square of the cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointPolarAngleGapUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurveEndpointRadiusIsLittleODistance
items.statement:
The squared cycle scale is little-o of the endpoint distance to the
limiting circle for every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointRadiusIsLittleODistance

items.label: slowCurveEndpointSubCenterLimit_ne_zero
items.statement: Every endpoint of a sufficiently small slow-curve orbit avoids each limiting center.
items.title: slowCurveEndpointSubCenterLimit_ne_zero

items.label: slowCurveEndpoint_injective
items.statement:
The flattened endpoint sequence of every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve
orbit is injective once its center and amplitude have the stated limits.
items.title: slowCurveEndpoint_injective

items.label: slowCurveFirstStepNormRemainder
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the first
physical displacement divided by the amplitude differs from `2 * ε_j ^ 2` by
`o(ε_j ^ 2)`.
items.title: slowCurveFirstStepNormRemainder

items.label: slowCurveFrameAngleIncrementUnique
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small exact invariant slow-curve orbit, every recursive
frame-angle difference is the unique small angle representing the relative frame.
items.title: slowCurveFrameAngleIncrementUnique

items.label: slowCurveFrameAngleRepresentsLowVector
items.statement:
Along a sufficiently small exact invariant slow-curve orbit, the accumulated frame
angle rotates the initial physical low vector to every cycle-boundary low vector.
items.title: slowCurveFrameAngleRepresentsLowVector

items.label: slowCurveFrameAngleTendstoAtBot
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the unwrapped physical
frame angle tends to negative infinity.
items.title: slowCurveFrameAngleTendstoAtBot

items.label: slowCurveFrameRotation
items.statement:
Along sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbits, the unwrapped physical
frame angle advances by `-3 * ε ^ 2` with a uniform fourth-order remainder.
items.title: slowCurveFrameRotation

items.label: slowCurveFullCenterDrift
items.statement:
Lemma 7 (`lem:two-step-expansions`), full-cycle center component.
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, one physical cycle
changes the center by `-(116 / 5) * G * ε ^ 6` times the physical low vector,
up to a vector remainder bounded by a constant multiple of `G * ε ^ 7`.
items.title: slowCurveFullCenterDrift

items.label: slowCurveFullCenterDriftBound
items.statement:
Any prescribed positive threshold below `1 / 4` admits a smaller threshold
with the same uniform full-cycle center-drift estimate.
items.title: slowCurveFullCenterDriftBound

items.label: slowCurveHalfCenterDisplacement
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the physical
first-half center displacement is bounded asymptotically by the amplitude times
the cube of the cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveHalfCenterDisplacement

items.label: slowCurveHalfCenterDisplacementBound
items.statement:
Along all sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbits, one positive
constant uniformly bounds every physical first-half center displacement by the
amplitude times the cube of the cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveHalfCenterDisplacementBound

items.label: slowCurveMiddleCenterTailIsBigO
items.statement:
For sufficiently small exact slow-curve orbits, intermediate centers
approach the cycle-boundary limit with cubic order in the cycle scale.
items.title: slowCurveMiddleCenterTailIsBigO

items.label: slowCurveNearReturnAmplitudeGap
items.statement:
Comparable-scale cycle endpoints whose lifted angles differ by a positive
number of windings have an amplitude gap bounded below by that winding count
times the squared incoming scale.
items.title: slowCurveNearReturnAmplitudeGap

items.label: slowCurveNearReturnCycleCountBound
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow curve, a positive near-return winding
across `N` cycles satisfies the uniform cycle-count inequality.
items.title: slowCurveNearReturnCycleCountBound

items.label: slowCurveNearReturnEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Comparable-scale positive-winding near returns on a sufficiently small invariant
slow curve have endpoint separation proportional to the earlier squared scale.
items.title: slowCurveNearReturnEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowCurveNearReturnWindingNumber_pos
items.statement:
A near-return decomposition of two lifted endpoint angles has positive winding
number when the later endpoint is chronologically and radially separated.
items.title: slowCurveNearReturnWindingNumber_pos

items.label: slowCurvePhaseCorrectionRatioUniformBound
items.statement:
Unbundled compatibility form of
`DFP.TwoLeg.SlowCurve.phaseCorrectionRatioUniformBound`.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseCorrectionRatioUniformBound

items.label: slowCurvePhaseDecreaseRatioLowerBound
items.statement: The uniform decrease-ratio estimate for an unbundled slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseDecreaseRatioLowerBound

items.label: slowCurvePhasePredictedDecreaseUniformBounds
items.statement:
Unbundled compatibility form of
`DFP.TwoLeg.SlowCurve.phasePredictedDecreaseUniformBounds`.
items.title: slowCurvePhasePredictedDecreaseUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorIsBigO
items.statement:
Both endpoint phases have radial error bounded by a cubic power of the
cycle scale along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorIsBigO

items.label: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorIsLittleO
items.statement:
Both endpoint phases have radial error little-o of the square of the
cycle scale along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorIsLittleO

items.label: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorUniform
items.statement:
A monotone right-hand modulus uniformly bounds both phase-radius errors by
the square of the cycle scale over all sufficiently small initial scales.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseRadiusErrorUniform

items.label: slowCurvePhaseStepNormUniformBounds
items.statement:
Unbundled compatibility form of
`DFP.TwoLeg.SlowCurve.phaseStepNormUniformBounds`.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseStepNormUniformBounds

items.label: slowCurvePhaseStepRatioUniformBound
items.statement:
Unbundled compatibility form of
`DFP.TwoLeg.SlowCurve.phaseStepRatioUniformBound`.
items.title: slowCurvePhaseStepRatioUniformBound

items.label: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorIsBigO
items.statement:
The lifted polar-to-gradient angle error is big-O of the cubic orbit scale
along every endpoint phase of a small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorIsBigO

items.label: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorIsLittleO
items.statement:
The lifted polar-to-gradient angle error is little-O of the quadratic orbit
scale along every endpoint phase of a small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorIsLittleO

items.label: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorUniform
items.statement:
A uniform cubic bound controls the lifted polar-to-gradient angle error on a
small invariant slow-curve orbit.
items.title: slowCurvePolarGradientAngleErrorUniform

items.label: slowCurveScalarAsymptotics
items.statement:
Lemma 8 (`lem:scalar-asymptotics`). A sufficiently small invariant slow-curve
orbit has the canonical scale,
amplitude, center, winding, and endpoint cluster-set asymptotics.
items.title: slowCurveScalarAsymptotics

items.label: slowCurveSecondStepNormRemainder
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the second
physical displacement divided by the amplitude differs from `ε_j ^ 2` by
`o(ε_j ^ 2)`.
items.title: slowCurveSecondStepNormRemainder

items.label: slowCurveTotalStepLengthNotSummable
items.statement:
Along every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit, the series of
the two physical displacement norms in each cycle is not summable.
items.title: slowCurveTotalStepLengthNotSummable

items.label: slowCurveUniformEndpointPairSeparation
items.statement:
All distinct endpoints of every sufficiently small invariant slow-curve orbit
are uniformly separated at the squared scale of the first endpoint.
items.title: slowCurveUniformEndpointPairSeparation

items.label: slowCurveUniformEndpointSeparation
items.statement:
Lemma 9 (`lem:separation`). Every endpoint of a sufficiently small invariant
slow-curve orbit is uniformly
isolated from all other endpoints and from the limiting circle at its squared scale.
items.title: slowCurveUniformEndpointSeparation

items.label: slowGradientNorms_eventually_mem_Icc
items.statement: Both normalized endpoint norms enter a fixed positive interval along a slow graph.
items.title: slowGradientNorms_eventually_mem_Icc

items.label: slowGraphPath_tendsto
items.statement:
The fifth-order slow-graph remainders force the parameter path to converge
to the canceled base state `(0, 2, 1)`. This is the unbundled compatibility
wrapper for `DFP.TwoLeg.SlowGraph.path_tendsto`.
items.title: slowGraphPath_tendsto

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_eventually_upper
items.statement:
Helper for an identity-initialized operator certificate has a positive gradient
`liminf` once its recorded eventual lower bound is supplemented by an
eventual finite upper bound.  The extra hypothesis is explicit because a
conditionally complete real `liminf` is not determined by a lower bound alone.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_eventually_upper

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_tendsto
items.statement:
Helper for an identity-initialized operator certificate whose transformed gradient norm
is known to converge has the paper-facing positive `liminf` conclusion.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_tendsto

items.label: initialInverseHessian_is_identity
items.statement:
Helper for the identity-initialized operator certificate exposes its exact initial
inverse-Hessian identity as a direct semantic projection.
items.title: initialInverseHessian_is_identity

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_eventually_upper
items.statement:
Helper for a strong identity-initialized operator certificate has the same semantic
`liminf` projection, under the explicit eventual upper bound required by the
real-valued liminf construction.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_eventually_upper

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_tendsto
items.statement:
Helper for the strong identity-initialized operator certificate has the same `liminf`
projection when its transformed gradient norm is supplied with a positive
limit.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos_of_tendsto

items.label: initialInverseHessian_is_identity
items.statement:
Helper for the strong identity-initialized certificate preserves the exact initial
inverse-Hessian identity from its underlying operator certificate.
items.title: initialInverseHessian_is_identity

items.label: gradientNorm_liminf_pos
items.statement: The matrix certificate has a positive gradient-norm liminf.
items.title: gradientNorm_liminf_pos

items.label: hessianBounds_pos_le
items.statement: The matrix certificate has ordered positive Hessian bounds.
items.title: hessianBounds_pos_le

items.label: ofOperator
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: an identity-initialized operator certificate
with positive-definite matrices, nonzero secant denominators, and a positive gradient
liminf yields the corresponding matrix certificate.
items.title: ofOperator

items.label: ofOperatorWithObjective
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: the operator-to-matrix bridge
retains the objective exactly, preserving its analytic regularity.
items.title: ofOperatorWithObjective

items.label: ofOperator_ofIdentityAndSecantCurvature
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: identity initialization and positive secant
curvature yield a matrix certificate with a positive gradient liminf, without requiring
convergence of the gradient norms.
items.title: ofOperator_ofIdentityAndSecantCurvature

items.label: ofOperator_ofSecantCurvature
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: positive secant curvature supplies the
nonzero denominators required by the matrix liminf certificate.
items.title: ofOperator_ofSecantCurvature

items.label: gradientNormLiminf_pos
items.statement: The positive gradient-norm limit of a matrix certificate is also its filter liminf.
items.title: gradientNormLiminf_pos

items.label: ofOperator
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: an operator certificate with positive-definite
canonical matrices and nonzero secant denominators yields a matrix identity certificate.
items.title: ofOperator

items.label: ofOperator_ofIdentityAndSecantCurvature
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: identity initialization and positive secant
curvature give positive-definite matrices and a matrix identity certificate.
items.title: ofOperator_ofIdentityAndSecantCurvature

items.label: ofOperator_ofSecantCurvature
items.statement:
Helper for cor:identity-initialization: positive secant curvature supplies the
nonzero denominators required by the matrix identity certificate.
items.title: ofOperator_ofSecantCurvature

items.label: canonicalMatrixSequence_apply
items.statement:
Evaluation of the canonical matrix representation at
an iteration index.
items.title: canonicalMatrixSequence_apply

items.label: canonicalMatrixSequence_denominator_ne_of_operatorOrbit
items.statement:
A strictly positive secant pairing along an operator orbit supplies the
nonzero denominator for its canonical matrix orbit.
items.title: canonicalMatrixSequence_denominator_ne_of_operatorOrbit

items.label: canonicalMatrixSequence_eq_explicit
items.statement:
Identify the canonical matrix sequence with its
explicit `Matrix.toEuclideanCLM.symm` pointwise representation.
items.title: canonicalMatrixSequence_eq_explicit
