Supporting fact: the replacement jet has exactly the
requested coefficient at its top order.
items.title: replaceTopCoeff_coeff_top

items.label: scalarCoeff_apply
items.statement:
A scalar jet coefficient is its multilinear coefficient evaluated on the
all-ones vector.
items.title: scalarCoeff_apply

items.label: scalarCoeff_eq_of_eval_sub_isLittleO
items.statement:
If the diagonal evaluations of two one-variable jets differ by `o(h ^ m)`,
then all of their scalar coefficients through degree `m` agree.
items.title: scalarCoeff_eq_of_eval_sub_isLittleO

items.label: scalarCoeff_ofFunction
items.statement:
The scalar coefficients of `ofFunction` are normalized iterated
one-variable derivatives.
items.title: scalarCoeff_ofFunction

items.label: sqrt_def
items.statement: Square-root jets are obtained by postcomposition with `Real.sqrt`.
items.title: sqrt_def

items.label: toFormalMultilinearSeries_coeff_of_le
items.statement:
The zero extension agrees with the jet coefficient in every degree at most
`m`.
items.title: toFormalMultilinearSeries_coeff_of_le

items.label: toFormalMultilinearSeries_coeff_of_lt
items.statement:
The formal multilinear series associated to a finite jet vanishes in every
degree strictly above `m`.
items.title: toFormalMultilinearSeries_coeff_of_lt

items.label: uniformCoeffBounds_of_contDiffAt
items.statement:
Pointwise joint `C^m` regularity on a compact parameter set gives one
uniform norm bound for every factorial-normalized Taylor coefficient.
items.title: uniformCoeffBounds_of_contDiffAt

items.label: uniformJetData_of_contDiffAt
items.statement:
The compact-fiber coefficient bounds and the standard uniform remainder
estimate can be consumed together as the two clauses of a uniform jet proof.
items.title: uniformJetData_of_contDiffAt

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_analyticAt
items.statement:
If a family is jointly analytic at every point of a compact parameter
fiber, its factorial-normalized finite Taylor jets have a uniform Peano
remainder bound there.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_analyticAt

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_analyticOnNhd
items.statement:
A jointly analytic family has factorial-normalized order-`m` Taylor jets
whose Peano remainders satisfy every positive order-`m` coefficient bound uniformly on
a compact parameter set.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_analyticOnNhd

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_contDiff
items.statement:
A jointly `C^m` family has factorial-normalized order-`m` Taylor jets whose
Peano remainders satisfy every positive order-`m` coefficient bound uniformly on a
compact parameter set.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_contDiff

items.label: uniformRemainderOn_of_contDiffAt
items.statement:
If a family is jointly `C^m` at every point of a compact parameter fiber,
its factorial-normalized order-`m` Taylor jets have a uniform Peano remainder
bound there.
items.title: uniformRemainderOn_of_contDiffAt

items.label: uniform_orderFive_bound_of_zero_fourJet
items.statement:
A jointly `C⁵` scalar-path family whose order-four jets vanish has a
uniform fifth-order norm bound on every compact parameter set.
items.title: uniform_orderFive_bound_of_zero_fourJet

items.label: weighted_transverse_isBigO
items.statement:
If two parameter paths differ by `O(a)` and the derivative of every fixed-index
slice is uniformly `O(b)` along the segment joining them, then their images differ
by `O(a * b)`.  This is the integral-free mean-value form of weighted transverse
transport.
items.title: weighted_transverse_isBigO

items.label: weighted_transverse_pow_isBigO
items.statement:
Power-law specialization of `weighted_transverse_isBigO`: an `O(ε^m)`
path perturbation and an `O(ε^k)` slice derivative produce an
`O(ε^(m+k))` image perturbation.
items.title: weighted_transverse_pow_isBigO

items.label: div_eq_div_of_eq_pow_mul
items.statement:
Exact factorizations by a common power have equal residual and original quotients
away from zero.
items.title: div_eq_div_of_eq_pow_mul

items.label: exists_norm_fderiv_le
items.statement:
The first derivative of a compactly supported `C^1` function admits a nonnegative
global operator-norm bound.
items.title: exists_norm_fderiv_le

items.label: exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_le
items.statement:
Every fixed iterated derivative of a compactly supported `C^n` function admits a
nonnegative global norm bound.
items.title: exists_norm_iteratedFDeriv_le

items.label: exists_norm_secondFDeriv_le
items.statement:
The second derivative of a compactly supported `C^2` function admits a nonnegative
global operator-norm bound.
items.title: exists_norm_secondFDeriv_le

items.label: indicator_compl_of_mem
items.statement:
At a point in the complement of a closed set, extending a function by zero across the
set preserves its certified Frechet derivative.
items.title: indicator_compl_of_mem

items.label: contDiff_update_succ_top
items.statement: The updated Taylor witness immediately gives finite smoothness of the updated function.
items.title: contDiff_update_succ_top

items.label: update_succ_top
items.statement:
Supporting fact: (finite-smooth invariant graph): replace only the
top formal Taylor term while retaining a predecessor Taylor series.
items.title: update_succ_top

items.label: comp_continuousLinearEquiv
items.statement: A certified gradient pulls back by the adjoint of a continuous linear equivalence.
items.title: comp_continuousLinearEquiv

items.label: indicator_compl_of_mem
items.statement:
At a point in the complement of a closed set, extending a scalar function by zero
across the set preserves its certified gradient.
items.title: indicator_compl_of_mem

items.label: at
items.statement: A global Hessian bound specializes at every point.
items.title: at

items.label: comp_continuousLinearEquiv
items.statement: Relative norm bounds on a coordinate map transport global Hessian bounds.
items.title: comp_continuousLinearEquiv

items.label: comp_linearIsometryEquiv
items.statement: Hessian bounds are invariant under an isometric linear change of coordinates.
items.title: comp_linearIsometryEquiv

items.label: of_forall
items.statement: Pointwise Hessian bounds at every point assemble into a global Hessian bound.
items.title: of_forall

items.label: comp_continuousLinearEquiv
items.statement: Relative norm bounds on a coordinate map transport pointwise Hessian bounds.
items.title: comp_continuousLinearEquiv

items.label: of_quadraticForm
items.statement:
A self-adjoint Hessian satisfying quadratic-form inequalities has the corresponding
Loewner bounds.
items.title: of_quadraticForm

items.label: quadraticForm
items.statement: Loewner Hessian bounds imply the corresponding quadratic-form inequalities.
items.title: quadraticForm

items.label: contDiffAt_halfNormSq_sub_add
items.statement:
Adding a twice continuously differentiable perturbation to half the squared distance
preserves twice continuous differentiability at the base point.
items.title: contDiffAt_halfNormSq_sub_add

items.label: fderiv_gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add
items.statement:
The Hessian of a translated squared norm plus a twice continuously differentiable
perturbation is the identity operator plus the perturbation Hessian.
items.title: fderiv_gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add

items.label: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add
items.statement:
The gradient of a translated squared norm plus a differentiable perturbation is the
displacement vector plus the perturbation gradient.
items.title: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add

items.label: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hasGradientAt
items.statement:
Under a perturbation gradient certificate, the canonical gradient of the translated
quadratic plus the perturbation is the displacement plus the certified gradient.
items.title: gradient_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hasGradientAt

items.label: halfNormSq_sub_add_apply_of_eq_zero
items.statement:
A perturbation value that vanishes at a point leaves the translated quadratic value
unchanged there.
items.title: halfNormSq_sub_add_apply_of_eq_zero

items.label: hasGradientAt_halfNormSq_sub_add
items.statement:
A certified perturbation gradient adds to the displacement gradient of the translated
quadratic base.
items.title: hasGradientAt_halfNormSq_sub_add

items.label: hasHessianBoundsAt_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hessian_norm_le
items.statement:
An operator-norm bound on a perturbation Hessian gives pointwise two-sided Loewner
bounds for half the squared distance plus that perturbation.
items.title: hasHessianBoundsAt_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hessian_norm_le

items.label: hasHessianBounds_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hessian_norm_le
items.statement:
A uniform perturbation-Hessian norm bound gives global two-sided Loewner bounds for
half the squared distance plus the perturbation.
items.title: hasHessianBounds_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_hessian_norm_le

items.label: hasHessianBounds_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_secondFDeriv_norm_le
items.statement:
A uniform bound on the ordinary second Frechet derivative can be consumed directly as
global two-sided Hessian bounds for a quadratic base plus a perturbation.
items.title: hasHessianBounds_halfNormSq_sub_add_of_secondFDeriv_norm_le

items.label: hessian_halfNormSq_sub_add
items.statement:
The Hessian of half the squared distance plus a `C²` perturbation is the identity
operator plus the perturbation Hessian.
items.title: hessian_halfNormSq_sub_add

items.label: strongConvexOn_halfNormSq_add_of_hessian_norm_le
items.statement:
A global Hessian norm bound below one makes a quadratic base plus the perturbation
strongly convex with the reduced modulus `1 - η`.
items.title: strongConvexOn_halfNormSq_add_of_hessian_norm_le

items.label: strongConvexOn_halfNormSq_add_of_secondFDeriv_norm_le
items.statement:
The same strong-convexity conclusion can be consumed directly from a uniform bound
on the ordinary second Fréchet derivative of the perturbation.
items.title: strongConvexOn_halfNormSq_add_of_secondFDeriv_norm_le

items.label: contDiff_two_indicator_compl
items.statement:
A twice continuously differentiable function off a closed set extends by zero to a
globally twice continuously differentiable function when its value, first derivative, and
second derivative vanish at the corresponding distance-scaled rates.
items.title: contDiff_two_indicator_compl

items.label: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl
items.statement:
If a function and its first derivative decay at the required rates toward a closed set,
then the second derivative of its extension by zero is the extension by zero of its second
derivative.
items.title: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl

items.label: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero
items.statement:
The second Fréchet derivative of a zero extension vanishes identically on the closed
set when the source value and first derivative have the required second-order decay.
items.title: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero

items.label: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem
items.statement:
A zero extension has vanishing second Fréchet derivative at every point of the closed
set when the source value and first derivative satisfy the second-order extension decay.
items.title: fderiv_fderiv_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem

items.label: fderiv_indicator_compl
items.statement:
The derivative of the extension by zero off a closed set agrees with the extension of
the derivative when the function is differentiable off the set and decays faster than the
distance to the set.
items.title: fderiv_indicator_compl

items.label: fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero
items.statement:
The first derivative of a zero extension vanishes identically on the closed set when
the source function has the required first-order distance decay.
items.title: fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero

items.label: fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero_of_quadratic_value_decay
items.statement:
Quadratic value decay is sufficient for the first derivative of a zero extension to
vanish identically on the closed set.
items.title: fderiv_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero_of_quadratic_value_decay

items.label: fderiv_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem
items.statement:
A zero extension has vanishing first derivative at every point of the closed set
when the source function has the distance-scaled value decay required for extension.
items.title: fderiv_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem

items.label: gradient_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero
items.statement:
The gradient of a scalar-valued zero extension vanishes identically on the closed set
when the source function has the required first-order distance decay.
items.title: gradient_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero

items.label: gradient_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero_of_quadratic_value_decay
items.statement:
Quadratic value decay is sufficient for the gradient of a scalar-valued zero extension
to vanish identically on the closed set.
items.title: gradient_indicator_compl_eqOn_zero_of_quadratic_value_decay

items.label: gradient_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem
items.statement:
A zero extension has zero Euclidean gradient at every point of the closed set under the
same first-order value decay hypothesis.
items.title: gradient_indicator_compl_eq_zero_of_mem

items.label: union_range_of_mapClusterPt
items.statement:
A closed set containing every `atTop` cluster point of a sequence remains closed after
adjoining the sequence's range.
items.title: union_range_of_mapClusterPt

items.label: comp_continuousLinearEquiv
items.statement:
Helper for Strong-Wolfe endpoint certificates pull back through an
arbitrary continuous linear equivalence when the transformed gradients are
used, not only through an isometry.
items.title: comp_continuousLinearEquiv

items.label: comp_linearIsometryEquiv
items.statement:
Pulling back a strong-Wolfe step through a linear isometry
equivalence preserves endpoint gradients and absolute curvature.
items.title: comp_linearIsometryEquiv

items.label: ofHasGradientAt
items.statement:
Certified endpoint gradients and strong curvature construct the
gradient-based strong-Wolfe predicate.
items.title: ofHasGradientAt

items.label: orthogonalSum_iff
items.statement:
The gradient-based strong-Wolfe predicate is invariant under an
orthogonal-sum quadratic extension.
items.title: orthogonalSum_iff

items.label: toWeakWolfe
items.statement:
Strong curvature gives weak curvature when the initial directional
derivative is nonpositive.
items.title: toWeakWolfe

items.label: coefficientBounds
items.statement: Weak Wolfe coefficients satisfy their three strict ordering bounds.
items.title: coefficientBounds

items.label: comp_linearIsometryEquiv
items.statement:
The gradient-based weak Wolfe conditions are invariant under an isometric
linear change of coordinates.
items.title: comp_linearIsometryEquiv

items.label: differentiableAtEndpoints
items.statement: Weak Wolfe satisfaction includes differentiability at both endpoints of the step.
items.title: differentiableAtEndpoints

items.label: directionalDerivative_lt_next
items.statement: Along a descent step, weak curvature strictly increases the directional derivative.
items.title: directionalDerivative_lt_next

items.label: iff
items.statement:
Weak Wolfe satisfaction is equivalent to its coefficient, differentiability, Armijo,
and weak-curvature conditions.
items.title: iff

items.label: inequalities
items.statement: Weak Wolfe satisfaction supplies the Armijo and weak-curvature inequalities.
items.title: inequalities

items.label: ofHasGradientAtSelectedConstants
items.statement:
Certified endpoint gradients and the two line-search inequalities establish weak
Wolfe satisfaction for the selected coefficients `1 / 4` and `3 / 4`.
items.title: ofHasGradientAtSelectedConstants

items.label: orthogonalSum_iff
items.statement:
Weak Wolfe satisfaction for an embedded step is equivalent to weak Wolfe satisfaction
in the original coordinate summand.
items.title: orthogonalSum_iff

items.label: secantCurvature_pos
items.statement: Along a descent step, the gradient displacement has positive pairing with the step.
items.title: secantCurvature_pos

items.label: selectedConstantsAdmissible
items.statement:
The coefficients `1 / 4` and `3 / 4` satisfy the strict bounds required for weak
Wolfe line search.
items.title: selectedConstantsAdmissible

items.label: c₁_lt_one
items.statement: The first coefficient in an admissible Wolfe pair is less than one.
items.title: c₁_lt_one

items.label: c₁_nonneg
items.statement: The first coefficient in an admissible Wolfe pair is nonnegative.
items.title: c₁_nonneg

items.label: c₂_nonneg
items.statement: The second coefficient in an admissible Wolfe pair is nonnegative.
items.title: c₂_nonneg

items.label: c₂_pos
items.statement: The second coefficient in an admissible Wolfe pair is positive.
items.title: c₂_pos

items.label: of_decreaseRatio
items.statement:
A normalized objective decrease proves the scalar Armijo condition along a descent
direction.
items.title: of_decreaseRatio

items.label: comp_continuousLinearEquiv_iff
items.statement: Strong Wolfe satisfaction is unchanged by pulling an objective back along an equivalence.
items.title: comp_continuousLinearEquiv_iff

items.label: comp_iff
items.statement: Pulling an objective back by a linear map preserves strong Wolfe satisfaction.
items.title: comp_iff

items.label: map_iff
items.statement:
Strong Wolfe satisfaction is invariant under a linear map on whose range the objectives
agree.
items.title: map_iff

items.label: ofHasGradientAt
items.statement: Certified endpoint gradients construct strong Wolfe satisfaction.
items.title: ofHasGradientAt

items.label: ofHasLineDerivAt
items.statement: Certified endpoint line derivatives construct strong Wolfe satisfaction.
items.title: ofHasLineDerivAt

items.label: toIsWeakWolfe
items.statement:
A strong directional-derivative certificate with certified endpoint gradients yields the
legacy gradient-based weak-Wolfe predicate along a nonascending direction.
items.title: toIsWeakWolfe

items.label: toWeak
items.statement: Strong Wolfe satisfaction becomes weak Wolfe satisfaction along a nonascending step.
items.title: toWeak

items.label: of_eq_mul
items.statement: Multiplicative control of the next slope proves strong curvature.
items.title: of_eq_mul

items.label: weak
items.statement: Strong curvature implies weak curvature along a nonascending direction.
items.title: weak

items.label: comp_continuousLinearEquiv_iff
items.statement: Weak Wolfe satisfaction is unchanged by pulling an objective back along an equivalence.
items.title: comp_continuousLinearEquiv_iff

items.label: comp_iff
items.statement: Pulling an objective back by a linear map preserves weak Wolfe satisfaction.
items.title: comp_iff

items.label: map_iff
items.statement:
Weak Wolfe satisfaction is invariant under a linear map on whose range the objectives
agree.
items.title: map_iff

items.label: ofHasGradientAt
items.statement: Certified endpoint gradients construct weak Wolfe satisfaction.
items.title: ofHasGradientAt

items.label: ofHasLineDerivAt
items.statement: Certified endpoint line derivatives construct weak Wolfe satisfaction.
items.title: ofHasLineDerivAt

items.label: ofIsWeakWolfe
items.statement: A gradient-based weak-Wolfe certificate yields the directional-derivative formulation.
items.title: ofIsWeakWolfe

items.label: secantSlope_pos
items.statement: Along a descent step, weak Wolfe curvature makes the secant slope positive.
items.title: secantSlope_pos

items.label: slope_lt_next
items.statement: Weak Wolfe curvature strictly increases a strictly negative endpoint slope.
items.title: slope_lt_next

items.label: toIsWeakWolfe
items.statement:
A directional weak-Wolfe certificate and certified endpoint gradients yield the legacy
gradient-based weak-Wolfe predicate.
items.title: toIsWeakWolfe

items.label: isArmijo_iff
items.statement: The scalar Armijo predicate unfolds to its defining inequality.
items.title: isArmijo_iff

items.label: isStrongCurvature_iff
items.statement: The scalar strong-curvature predicate unfolds to its defining inequality.
items.title: isStrongCurvature_iff

items.label: isWeakCurvature_iff
items.statement: The scalar weak-curvature predicate unfolds to its defining inequality.
items.title: isWeakCurvature_iff

items.label: lineDeriv_map
items.statement: Restricting an objective along a linear map preserves its endpoint line derivative.
items.title: lineDeriv_map

items.label: lineDifferentiable_map_iff
items.statement: Line differentiability is preserved when two objectives agree after a linear map.
items.title: lineDifferentiable_map_iff

items.label: armijo_of_decrease_ratio_lower_bound
items.statement:
A lower bound on a normalized scalar decrease yields the corresponding Armijo
inequality whenever the directional pairing is the negative predicted decrease.
items.title: armijo_of_decrease_ratio_lower_bound

items.label: armijo_of_function_decrease_ratio_lower_bound
items.statement:
A normalized objective decrease bound gives Armijo for a function and a certified
directional pairing at the initial endpoint.
items.title: armijo_of_function_decrease_ratio_lower_bound

items.label: armijo_of_half_decrease_ratio
items.statement: The standard `q = -⟪g, s⟫` presentation of the half-decrease Armijo bridge.
items.title: armijo_of_half_decrease_ratio

items.label: armijo_of_half_function_decrease_ratio
items.statement:
A half-unit normalized decrease is enough for Armijo with the standard coefficient
`c₁ = 1 / 4`.
items.title: armijo_of_half_function_decrease_ratio

items.label: adaptedRate_lt
items.statement: The adapted rate is strictly below the proposed contraction bound.
items.title: adaptedRate_lt

items.label: adaptedSeminorm_isContracting
items.statement: The weighted-iterate seminorm makes `L` contract with a coefficient below `r`.
items.title: adaptedSeminorm_isContracting

items.label: adaptedSeminorm_isEquivalent
items.statement: The weighted-iterate seminorm is equivalent to the ambient norm.
items.title: adaptedSeminorm_isEquivalent

items.label: adaptedSeminorm_spec
items.statement:
If the complex spectral radius of a real endomorphism is below `r < 1`, then its
weighted-iterate seminorm is equivalent to the ambient norm and contracts it below `r`.
items.title: adaptedSeminorm_spec

items.label: eq_id_of_abs_ge
items.statement:
A compactly supported cutoff has a common bounded interval outside which every
center projection along a uniformly bounded small graph is the identity.
items.title: eq_id_of_abs_ge

items.label: inverse_def
items.statement:
The center-projection inverse is definitionally the inverse selected by
`Function.invFun`.
items.title: inverse_def

items.label: map_apply
items.statement:
The center projection evaluates as the first coordinate of the cutoff-modified
center-stable map along the graph.
items.title: map_apply

items.label: contractingWith
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a pointwise bounded-section certificate yields the
canonical `ContractingWith` structure used by Mathlib's fixed-point API.
items.title: contractingWith

items.label: existsUnique_fixedSection
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the contraction certificate gives existence and uniqueness of a
bounded fixed section, without committing to a source-specific formula for the operator.
items.title: existsUnique_fixedSection

items.label: contDiff_succ_and_eq_iteratedFDeriv
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the projected holonomic top-section data supplies
successor smoothness and the corresponding iterated derivative identification.
items.title: contDiff_succ_and_eq_iteratedFDeriv

items.label: contDiff_succ_and_fixedSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the fixed graph context simultaneously supplies
successor smoothness and identifies its stored section with the next derivative.
items.title: contDiff_succ_and_fixedSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv

items.label: fixedSection_derivative
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the secant certificate in a fixed graph
context supplies the predecessor derivative equation for its stored section.
items.title: fixedSection_derivative

items.label: fixedSection_eq_canonical
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the fixed section stored in a graph context is the
canonical contraction fixed point for its recorded operator data.
items.title: fixedSection_eq_canonical

items.label: predecessor_iteratedDeriv_contDiff_one
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the secant certificate makes the scalar predecessor
coefficient `iteratedDeriv (r - 1) ζ` continuously differentiable to first order.
items.title: predecessor_iteratedDeriv_contDiff_one

items.label: contDiff_one
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a fixed-section secant certificate with a bounded continuous
limit section upgrades its map to a globally first-order continuously differentiable map.
items.title: contDiff_one

items.label: hasDerivAt
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the fixed-section secant certificate supplies the
pointwise derivative equation for its limiting section.
items.title: hasDerivAt

items.label: isLittleO_shift
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the fixed-section derivative certificate exposes
the translated little-o remainder in the form used by Fréchet derivative criteria.
items.title: isLittleO_shift

items.label: contDiff_succ_and_fixedSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the certificate simultaneously supplies the
successor smoothness and the iterated-derivative transport for its fixed section.
items.title: contDiff_succ_and_fixedSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv

items.label: fixedSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the holonomic fixed top section is the next
iterated derivative of the underlying graph.
items.title: fixedSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv

items.label: contDiff_succ_and_eq_iteratedFDeriv
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: holonomic predecessor data upgrades a graph by one smoothness
order and identifies the new section with the corresponding iterated derivative.
items.title: contDiff_succ_and_eq_iteratedFDeriv

items.label: continuous_topUpdatedGraphJet_coeff
items.statement:
Replacing the top coefficient by a bounded continuous section preserves
coefficientwise continuity of a bounded graph jet.
items.title: continuous_topUpdatedGraphJet_coeff

items.label: differentiatedJet_bddAbove
items.statement:
Under the finite-order smoothness and inverse-center hypotheses, every
coefficient family of the differentiated jet is bounded.
items.title: differentiatedJet_bddAbove

items.label: differentiatedJet_coeff_le
items.statement: The supremum bound contains every coefficient of the differentiated jet.
items.title: differentiatedJet_coeff_le

items.label: differentiatedJet_constantCoeff
items.statement:
The constant coefficient of the differentiated jet is the ordinary graph
transform evaluated at the same center parameter.
items.title: differentiatedJet_constantCoeff

items.label: existsUnique_fixedPoint_topSectionOperator
items.statement: A contracted transformed-top operator has a unique bounded continuous fixed section.
items.title: existsUnique_fixedPoint_topSectionOperator

items.label: finiteComposition_nonOnes_uniformBoundOn
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: a finite family of compact-uniform linear branch bounds
has one common radius for the non-distinguished composition sum.
items.title: finiteComposition_nonOnes_uniformBoundOn

items.label: map_spec
items.statement:
The bounded jet transform has the ordinary graph transform as its base graph
and the differentiated composition formula as its jet family.
items.title: map_spec

items.label: norm_coeff_sub_le_coeffDistance
items.statement:
Every pointwise coefficient distance is bounded by the corresponding
uniform distance between two bounded graph jets.
items.title: norm_coeff_sub_le_coeffDistance

items.label: topCoeff_contraction
items.statement:
If lower-order coefficients agree, the differentiated graph transform
contracts the top order by `rate * lower⁻¹ ^ r`.
items.title: topCoeff_contraction

items.label: topSectionOperator_apply
items.statement: Evaluation of the bundled top-section operator is the transformed top coefficient.
items.title: topSectionOperator_apply

items.label: topSectionValue_norm_le
items.statement: The stored bound of the transformed jet uniformly bounds its top-section value.
items.title: topSectionValue_norm_le

items.label: topUpdatedFiniteJet_coeff_le
items.statement:
The updated coefficient family is bounded by the old bounds below the top

items.label: fixedSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv_of_fixedGraphJetContexts

items.label: hasFDerivAt_of_isLittleO_shift_bridge

Every coefficient of a holonomic graph jet is the factorial-normalized

The top coefficient of a holonomic bounded graph jet is the normalized

items.label: isLittleO_of_norm_le_const_mul_add

items.label: isLittleO_shift_of_uniform_remainder

Supporting fact: a uniform translated-remainder estimate gives the
corresponding little-o statement at each base point.
items.title: isLittleO_shift_of_uniform_remainder

items.label: map_apply
items.statement: The cone-valued graph transform evaluates to the inverse-center pointwise formula.
items.title: map_apply

items.label: map_spec

The cone-valued graph transform satisfies the origin, radius, and Lipschitz
constraints.
items.title: map_spec

items.label: predecessorHasDerivAt_of_rawDefectLittleO
items.statement:
A translated first-order remainder that is little-o of its scalar increment
determines the corresponding derivative at every base point.
items.title: predecessorHasDerivAt_of_rawDefectLittleO

items.label: radiusEnvelope_sublinear_of_recurrence

recurrence is sublinear at zero when the weighted transport factor is below
one.
items.title: radiusEnvelope_sublinear_of_recurrence

items.label: rate_def

The contraction coefficient is the sum of the direct stable term and the term caused
by variation of the inverse center parameter.
items.title: rate_def

items.label: rawDefect_isLittleO_of_inverseRecurrence
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: a locally uniformly bounded raw defect satisfying a uniformly
small inverse-coordinate affine recurrence is little-o of its scalar increment at every base
point, provided both the recurrence factor and its transported factor are strict contractions.
items.title: rawDefect_isLittleO_of_inverseRecurrence

items.label: raw_apply
items.statement:
The raw graph transform evaluates to the stable coordinate at the inverse center
parameter.
items.title: raw_apply

items.label: raw_continuous

The inverse-center graph-transform formula is continuous under the quantitative
Lipschitz hypotheses.
items.title: raw_continuous

items.label: raw_lipschitzWith
items.statement:
The inverse-center formula obeys the prescribed graph Lipschitz constant under the
split stable estimate.
items.title: raw_lipschitzWith

items.label: raw_norm_le
items.statement:
The stable block bound, the stable remainder bound, and the radius inequality give
the pointwise radius estimate for the raw graph transform.
items.title: raw_norm_le

items.label: raw_zero

If the nonlinear term fixes the origin, then the raw graph transform fixes the
origin.
items.title: raw_zero

items.label: tendsto_boundedSection_of_tendsto_operator_residual

vanishing operator residual into convergence toward its canonical fixed section.
items.title: tendsto_boundedSection_of_tendsto_operator_residual

items.label: toBoundedContinuousFunction_apply
items.statement:
The bounded continuous graph transform evaluates to the raw graph-transform
formula.
items.title: toBoundedContinuousFunction_apply

items.title: toBoundedContinuousFunction_norm_le

items.label: topSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv_of_derivative
items.statement:
Helper for Infrastructure C: a top section satisfying the predecessor
derivative equation is the unnormalised next iterated derivative of the graph.
items.title: topSection_eq_iteratedFDeriv_of_derivative

items.label: uniformTranslatedFirstOrderRemainderOn
items.statement:
First-order Taylor remainders of translated `C¹` functions are uniform
when their translation centers range over a compact set.
items.title: uniformTranslatedFirstOrderRemainderOn

items.label: centerStableLinearize_apply
items.statement:
The center-stable cutoff perturbation evaluates as its block-linear part plus the
rescaled cutoff remainder.
items.title: centerStableLinearize_apply

items.label: centerStableLinearize_eq_linear
items.statement:
Outside the topological support of the rescaled cutoff, the center-stable cutoff
perturbation equals its block-linear part.
items.title: centerStableLinearize_eq_linear

items.label: centerStableLinearize_eventuallyEq
items.statement:
A cutoff equal to one near zero makes the center-stable cutoff perturbation and the
original nonlinear center-stable map have the same germ at zero.
items.title: centerStableLinearize_eventuallyEq

items.label: centerStable_apply
items.statement: The center-stable block map sends `(u, z)` to `(u, L z)`.
items.title: centerStable_apply

items.label: contDiff_linearize
items.statement:
Local `C^ν` regularity on an open neighborhood of the rescaled cutoff support
suffices for the cutoff perturbation to be globally `C^ν`.
items.title: contDiff_linearize

items.label: exists_scale_norm_fderiv_remainder_le
items.statement:
Under explicit first-order remainder and derivative bounds, shrinking a compact
`C¹` cutoff makes the derivative of the cutoff remainder uniformly small.
items.title: exists_scale_norm_fderiv_remainder_le

items.label: fderiv_linearize_zero
items.statement:
If the nonlinear map has zero value and derivative at zero, then a differentiable
rescaled cutoff perturbation has derivative `A` there.
items.title: fderiv_linearize_zero

items.label: hasCompactSupport_remainder
items.statement:
A nonzero rescaling of a compactly supported cutoff produces a compactly supported
cutoff remainder.
items.title: hasCompactSupport_remainder

items.label: iteratedFDeriv_linearize_zero
items.statement:
Every iterated Fréchet derivative at zero is preserved by a cutoff equal to one
near zero.
items.title: iteratedFDeriv_linearize_zero

`x ↦ A x + N x`.
items.title: linearize_eq_add_of_mem_closedBall

items.label: linearize_eq_linear_of_outer_radius_le_norm
items.statement:
At and beyond the scaled outer radius, a cutoff perturbation agrees with its
linear part.
items.title: linearize_eq_linear_of_outer_radius_le_norm

items.label: linearize_eventuallyEq
items.statement:
A cutoff equal to one near zero makes the cutoff perturbation and the original
nonlinear map have the same germ at zero.
items.title: linearize_eventuallyEq

items.label: linearize_zero

items.title: linearize_zero

bunching inequalities.

items.label: rawTransform_continuous
items.statement: Supporting fact: the raw metric graph transform is continuous.

items.statement: The raw metric transform has its defining inverse-center formula.
items.title: rawTransform_eq

Supporting fact: the sharp raw-transform estimate and the cone inequality
show that the metric graph transform preserves the prescribed Lipschitz cone.
items.title: rawTransform_lipschitzWith

items.label: rawTransform_lipschitzWith_sharp
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the raw metric graph transform has the sharp Lipschitz
constant obtained from the stable linear rate, graph slope, remainder size, and inverse-center
bound.

items.label: rawTransform_zero

center parameter.

numerator-over-denominator bound, without assuming differentiability of the section.

items.label: abs_inv_metricOrderOneDenominator_le

reciprocal certified lower bound.

items.label: abs_inv_metricOrderOneDenominator_sub_le
items.statement:

`lower⁻² * epsilon` factor.
items.title: abs_inv_metricOrderOneDenominator_sub_le

Supporting fact: inverse-center transport contracts scalar increments by at
most `lower⁻¹`.

items.label: abs_metricOrderOneDenominator_sub_le
items.statement:
Supporting fact: candidate denominators vary by at most `epsilon` times
the pointwise slope difference.

The center coordinate along a graph is quantitatively injective when its
Lipschitz perturbation size leaves a positive lower bound.

items.title: bunching_linear_factor_nonneg

items.statement: `p·c = (rate · lower⁻ᵐ) · lower⁻¹ = rate · lower⁻⁽ᵐ⁺¹⁾ < 1`, from `h_bunching (m + 1)`.

items.label: centerFiberRemainder_contDiff
items.statement:
The fiber remainder coordinate `g u = (d.R (u, ζ u)).2` is `ContDiff ℝ m` whenever `ζ` is,
provided `m ≤ d.nu`.  Written as `Prod.snd ∘ d.R ∘ (fun u ↦ (u, ζ u))`.
items.title: centerFiberRemainder_contDiff

items.label: centerMapDeriv_sub_one_hasCompactSupport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the center derivative differs from one only on a compact
set controlled by the base projection of `tsupport d.R`.
items.title: centerMapDeriv_sub_one_hasCompactSupport

items.label: centerMap_add_metricOrderOneSourceIncrement
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the transported source endpoint maps exactly to the
translated output endpoint.
items.title: centerMap_add_metricOrderOneSourceIncrement

items.label: centerMap_antilipschitz
items.statement:
Step 2: the metric center coordinate is antilipschitz with the reciprocal lower rate.
Its global inverse is `lower⁻¹`-Lipschitz, so `dist u v ≤ lower⁻¹ · dist (centerMap u) (centerMap v)`,
which is exactly the antilipschitz bound with constant `d.lower⁻¹`.
items.title: centerMap_antilipschitz

items.label: centerMap_contDiff_of_prev
items.statement:
Step 1: the metric center coordinate is as smooth as the current graph iterate.  From
`ContDiff ℝ k ζ` (the induction hypothesis) and the ambient remainder smoothness, the center
map `u ↦ u + (R (u, ζ u)).1` is `ContDiff ℝ k`.
items.title: centerMap_contDiff_of_prev

items.label: centerMap_continuous
items.statement:
The center map `Φ = centerMap ζ` is continuous (it is `id + c` with `c` the continuous center
remainder coordinate; `ζ` is continuous).
items.title: centerMap_continuous

items.label: centerMap_deriv_inv_pow_abs_le
items.statement:
The reciprocal-power coefficient `a u := (deriv Φ u)⁻ᵐ` is bounded by `lower⁻ᵐ` in absolute
value.  Uses the lower bound `lower ≤ Φ′u` (`centerMap_deriv_lower_bound`, needs `ζ ∈ C¹`).
items.title: centerMap_deriv_inv_pow_abs_le

items.label: centerMap_deriv_inv_pow_continuous
items.statement:
The reciprocal-power coefficient `a u := (deriv Φ u)⁻ᵐ` is continuous.  For `m ≥ 1` this uses
that `Φ = centerMap ζ` is `C¹` (hence `deriv Φ` is continuous) whenever `ζ` is `C¹`; the coefficient
is `(deriv Φ ·)⁻¹ ^ m`, a continuous function of the (nonvanishing) continuous `deriv Φ`.
items.title: centerMap_deriv_inv_pow_continuous

items.label: centerMap_deriv_lower_bound
items.statement: The center-map derivative is bounded below by `lower > 0`.
items.title: centerMap_deriv_lower_bound

items.label: centerMap_deriv_ne_zero
items.statement: The center-map derivative is nonzero.
items.title: centerMap_deriv_ne_zero

items.label: centerMap_deriv_pos
items.statement: The center-map derivative is strictly positive (it is `≥ lower > 0`).
items.title: centerMap_deriv_pos

items.label: centerMap_eq_add_remainder
items.statement: The center map differs from the identity by the center remainder: `φ = id + c`.
items.title: centerMap_eq_add_remainder

items.label: centerMap_hasDerivAt
items.statement: The center map has derivative `1 + c' u` at every point (given `ζ` is `C¹`).
items.title: centerMap_hasDerivAt

items.label: centerMap_inverseCenter
items.statement: Supporting fact: the base inverse center maps back to its output center.
items.title: centerMap_inverseCenter

items.label: centerMap_taylor_uniform
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the center map has a globally uniform first-order Taylor
remainder.
items.title: centerMap_taylor_uniform

items.label: centerProjection_approximatesId
items.statement:
A Lipschitz perturbation along a graph of slope at most one makes its center
coordinate approximate the identity with the same Lipschitz constant.
items.title: centerProjection_approximatesId

items.label: centerRemainder_contDiff
items.statement: The center remainder coordinate `c u = (R (u, ζ u)).1` is `ContDiff ℝ m` for `m ≤ d.nu`.
items.title: centerRemainder_contDiff

items.label: centerRemainder_differentiableAt
items.statement: The center remainder coordinate is differentiable at every point, given `ζ` is `C¹`.
items.title: centerRemainder_differentiableAt

items.label: centerRemainder_lipschitz
items.statement: The center remainder coordinate `u ↦ (R (u, ζ u)).1` is `epsilon`-Lipschitz.
items.title: centerRemainder_lipschitz

items.label: centerRemainder_norm_deriv_le
items.statement: The scalar derivative of the center remainder coordinate has norm `≤ epsilon`.
items.title: centerRemainder_norm_deriv_le

items.label: contDiff_le_of_core
items.statement:
The finite-smoothness induction: from the core, `ζ ∈ C^r` for every `r ≤ d.nu`.  Order `m`'s
smoothness is established before order `m + 1`'s witness consumes it, so this is not circular.
items.title: contDiff_le_of_core

items.label: contDiff_one_of_hasDerivAt_continuous
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a pointwise derivative field that is continuous upgrades the
underlying scalar map to a globally first-order continuously differentiable map.
items.title: contDiff_one_of_hasDerivAt_continuous

items.label: contDiff_one_of_tendsto_boundedContinuousFunction_secant

Supporting fact: a bounded continuous secant family with a continuous limit
field yields first-order continuous differentiability when its scaled evaluations are the genuine
nonzero secants at every base point.
items.title: contDiff_one_of_tendsto_boundedContinuousFunction_secant

items.label: continuousAt_metricOrderTwoFrozenSourceDerivative
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the frozen source partial derivative is continuous at

Supporting fact: the numerator varies continuously with the source

Supporting fact: the stable first-slot derivative varies continuously

Supporting fact: for each fixed increment, the translated secant varies
continuously with its base point.
