items.label: continuous_topJetSectionValue
items.statement:
Continuity of `u ↦ topSectionValue m (v u)` reduces to continuity of `v`.  The map factors
through `piFieldEquiv` (a linear isometry equiv), `smulRight 1 ·` (a continuous linear map), and
`uncurryLeft` (the inverse leg of the curry isometry equiv).
items.title: continuous_topJetSectionValue

items.label: continuous_topSectionValue
items.statement:
Step 9: continuity of the section `u ↦ topSectionValue m (v u)` reduces to continuity of `v`.
The map factors as `v ↦ piFieldEquiv v ↦ smulRight 1 (·) ↦ ·.uncurryLeft`, each stage a continuous
(linear) construction.
items.title: continuous_topSectionValue

items.label: derivCenterFiber_apply
items.statement:
Supporting fact: applying `derivCenterFiber d ζ u` to `w` gives the
center component of `fderiv ℝ d.R (u, ζ u)` in the fiber direction `(0, w)`.
items.title: derivCenterFiber_apply

items.label: derivFiber_apply
items.statement:
Application form of `derivFiber`: `derivFiber d ζ u w = (fderiv R (u, ζ u) (0, w)).2`, i.e. the
second-slot column of the full derivative.  Exposed for downstream leaves that cannot unfold the
`derivFiber` definition across the module boundary.
items.title: derivFiber_apply

items.label: derivFiber_zero
items.statement:
At the origin, the fiber derivative of the remainder equals the stable block `L`: this is
the center-stable germ `F = centerStable L + O(‖x‖²)`, whose derivative at zero is
`centerStable L`, whose second column is exactly `L`.
items.title: derivFiber_zero

items.label: deriv_fiber_remainder_at_origin_eq_fiber
items.statement:
Supporting fact: at the origin, the center-slot term vanishes under the
center-stable derivative certificate, leaving the pure fiber derivative contribution.
items.title: deriv_fiber_remainder_at_origin_eq_fiber

items.label: deriv_fiber_remainder_eq_first_slot_add_fiber
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the first derivative of the fiber remainder along a graph splits into
the center-slot contribution and the fiber derivative applied to the graph derivative.
items.title: deriv_fiber_remainder_eq_first_slot_add_fiber

items.label: dist_invFun_centerProjection_le
items.statement:
Inverse center parameters for two small graphs differ by at most the
remainder rate times their uniform distance and the inverse lower bound.
items.title: dist_invFun_centerProjection_le

items.label: eventually_norm_fderiv_remainder_le_at_zero
items.statement:
Supporting fact: differentiability at the origin gives an arbitrarily
small normalized linearization error on a neighborhood of the origin.
items.title: eventually_norm_fderiv_remainder_le_at_zero

items.label: existsOfComplexSpectralRadiusLtOne
items.statement:
Lemma 5 (`lem:graph-transform`). A finite-dimensional center-stable map whose
stable derivative has complex spectral
radius below one admits a finite-smooth local forward-invariant graph tangent to the center
axis.
items.title: existsOfComplexSpectralRadiusLtOne

items.label: existsOfEquivalentContractingSeminorm
items.statement:
A finite-dimensional center-stable map admits a finite-smooth local forward-invariant
graph when its stable derivative contracts an equivalent seminorm at a rate below one.
items.title: existsOfEquivalentContractingSeminorm

items.label: existsOfNormLtOne
items.statement:
A finite-dimensional center-stable map whose stable derivative has norm less than one
admits a finite-smooth local forward-invariant graph tangent to the center axis.
items.title: existsOfNormLtOne

items.label: existsUnique_metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_fixedPoint
items.statement:
Supporting fact: first-order bunching gives a unique bounded continuous
fixed slope field in the prescribed closed ball.
items.title: existsUnique_metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_fixedPoint

items.label: exists_centerProjectionHomeomorph
items.statement:
A center coordinate that is a perturbation of the identity by a Lipschitz
constant below one is represented by a global homeomorphism.
items.title: exists_centerProjectionHomeomorph

items.label: exists_cocycle_remainder_form
items.statement:
**(A.3) Cocycle in `Rem`-form is available from the solved cocycle.**  Specializes
`iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_cocycle_solved` to exhibit the opaque remainder `Rem` consumed by
`subtracted_cocycle_changeOfVariables`: `Rem w` is exactly the fiber-remainder derivative minus the
Faà-di-Bruno `ζ`-remainder, scaled by `(Φ′w)⁻ᵐ`.  This packages the `(C)` bucket as a concrete but
still-unestimated field, so downstream `(B)/(C)` work operates on a named object.
items.title: exists_cocycle_remainder_form

items.label: exists_metricInvariantGraph_of_regularFixedPoint
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure (metric Picard certificate with a finite-smooth fixed graph): an
explicit metric contraction, a zero-derivative remainder certificate, and regularity of its
fixed point produce a finite-smooth invariant graph tangent to the center axis.
items.title: exists_metricInvariantGraph_of_regularFixedPoint

items.label: exists_metricIteratedDeriv_norm_bound
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the predecessor iterated derivative on a fixed graph has a
global norm bound.
items.title: exists_metricIteratedDeriv_norm_bound

items.label: exists_metricReservedTopDerivativeForcing_norm_bound
items.statement:
Supporting fact: compact support and continuity give a nonnegative uniform
bound for the differentiated affine forcing.
items.title: exists_metricReservedTopDerivativeForcing_norm_bound

items.label: exists_metricReservedTopForcing_norm_bound
items.statement:
Supporting fact: compact support and continuity give a nonnegative uniform
bound for the reserved-top forcing.
items.title: exists_metricReservedTopForcing_norm_bound

items.label: exists_norm_fderiv_remainder_le_at_zero
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the preceding normalized error estimate can be
expressed as a positive-radius ball bound.
items.title: exists_norm_fderiv_remainder_le_at_zero

items.label: exists_smallLipschitzCutoffRemainder
items.statement:
A zero-jet map that is smooth near the origin admits a globally smooth,
compactly supported cutoff with an arbitrarily small Lipschitz constant.
items.title: exists_smallLipschitzCutoffRemainder

items.label: fiber_atomic_isolate_one
items.statement:
**Bivariate linear isolation, order `m = 1`.** At a point where the graph is differentiable,
the atomic fiber term splits into the stable-coordinate first-slot part
`(∂₁R(u,ζu) • 1).2` and the fiber (second-slot) part
`derivFiber d ζ u (iteratedDeriv 1 ζ u)`. This is the chain rule for `G ∘ pair`
(`G = snd ∘ R`, `pair y = (y, ζ y)`), made explicit. The differentiability hypothesis is
necessary because `fderiv` is defined to be zero at a nondifferentiability point.
items.title: fiber_atomic_isolate_one

items.label: fiber_atomic_isolate_one_at_origin
items.statement:
Supporting fact: at the base point, the center-stable derivative
annihilates the stable-coordinate contribution to the order-one fiber atom.
items.title: fiber_atomic_isolate_one_at_origin

items.label: fiber_remainder_eventuallyEq_zero_of_pair_notMem_tsupport
items.statement:
On a neighbourhood of any `u` whose graph point `(u, ζ u)` is off `tsupport R`, the fiber
remainder `g` agrees with the zero function.
items.title: fiber_remainder_eventuallyEq_zero_of_pair_notMem_tsupport

items.label: finOne_pairwiseDisjoint
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a family indexed by `Fin 1` is pairwise disjoint on
distinct indices, since there are no distinct indices.
items.title: finOne_pairwiseDisjoint

items.label: finiteTaylorJet_one_remainder_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: an order-one derivative jet has the usual affine
Taylor remainder.
items.title: finiteTaylorJet_one_remainder_eq

items.label: fixedGraph_comp_eq
items.statement: The fixed-point equation packaged as an equality of scalar functions `ζ ∘ φ = L ∘ ζ + g`.
items.title: fixedGraph_comp_eq

items.label: fixedGraph_eventuallyEq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport
items.statement:
Off the (compact) support of `ζ`, the graph agrees with the zero function on a neighbourhood.
This is a purely topological consequence of `tsupport` being closed; no fixed-point data needed.
items.title: fixedGraph_eventuallyEq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport

items.label: fixedGraph_hasCompactSupport
items.statement:
The metric fixed graph has compact support (reproduced from `MetricFiniteSmooth` so the
top-section core can localize its obligations to a compact set).  Uses only fields of
`MetricGraphTransformData`.
items.title: fixedGraph_hasCompactSupport

items.label: fixedPoint_invariant_of_rightInverse
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a fixed point of an inverse-coordinate graph
transform satisfies the original parametrized invariant equation after the inverse
is cancelled.
items.title: fixedPoint_invariant_of_rightInverse

items.label: ftaylorSeries_eq_iteratedFDeriv
items.statement:
Definitional: the holonomic obligation's Taylor coefficient is the multilinear iterated
derivative.
items.title: ftaylorSeries_eq_iteratedFDeriv

items.label: hasDerivAt_inv_smul_quotient
items.statement:
Supporting fact: differentiating an inverse scalar times a vector can be
written in denominator-cancelled quotient form.
items.title: hasDerivAt_inv_smul_quotient

items.label: hasDerivAt_iteratedDeriv_of_notMem_tsupport
items.statement:
Off the support of `ζ`, every iterated derivative has derivative `0`.  This discharges the
top-section obligation on the complement of the compact support without any analytic work.
items.title: hasDerivAt_iteratedDeriv_of_notMem_tsupport

items.label: hasDerivAt_iteratedDeriv_of_onSupport
items.statement:
**Localization combinator.**  A candidate derivative field `v` that (a) witnesses the
`HasDerivAt` on `tsupport ζ` and (b) vanishes off `tsupport ζ` witnesses it everywhere.  The
off-support branch is discharged by `hasDerivAt_iteratedDeriv_of_notMem_tsupport` (derivative `0`)
together with `v u = 0`.
items.title: hasDerivAt_iteratedDeriv_of_onSupport

items.label: hasDerivAt_of_eventually_le_pos_neg
items.statement:
Step 5–6: a two-sided sublinear bound on the secant defect yields `HasDerivAt`.  The two
hypotheses are exactly the positive- and negative-increment envelope outputs (each phrased as
an eventual bound on the one-sided neighborhood filter).
items.title: hasDerivAt_of_eventually_le_pos_neg

items.label: hasDerivAt_of_secant_bounds
items.statement:
Supporting fact: explicit positive and negative secant radii are
converted into the two one-sided filter bounds needed for a derivative at u₀.
items.title: hasDerivAt_of_secant_bounds

items.label: hasDerivAt_of_tendsto_boundedContinuousFunction_secant
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a convergent BoundedContinuousFunction-valued secant,
after fixed-point evaluation and constant scaling, yields the derivative of the underlying map.
items.title: hasDerivAt_of_tendsto_boundedContinuousFunction_secant

items.label: hasDerivAt_of_tendsto_normalized_secant
items.statement:
Supporting fact: convergence of a normalized secant model at zero gives the
derivative once the model agrees with the genuine secant at every nonzero increment.
items.title: hasDerivAt_of_tendsto_normalized_secant

items.label: hasFDerivAt_iteratedFDeriv_of_hasDerivAt
items.statement:
Step 7–8: a scalar derivative of the top jet upgrades to the multilinear holonomic
obligation.  `A u := (topSectionValue m (v u)).curryLeft` is the required Fréchet derivative of
`y ↦ iteratedFDeriv ℝ m ζ y` at `u`.
items.title: hasFDerivAt_iteratedFDeriv_of_hasDerivAt

items.label: hasFDerivAt_iteratedFDeriv_of_secant_bounds
items.statement:
Supporting fact: explicit two-sided secant bounds on the scalar
`m`-th iterated derivative produce the curried Fréchet derivative required by a holonomic
top section.
items.title: hasFDerivAt_iteratedFDeriv_of_secant_bounds

items.label: invariantGraph_of_metricFixedPoint_germ
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure (metric Picard germ transfer): the preceding invariant graph transfers
from the metric model to any original map with the same germ at the fixed point.
items.title: invariantGraph_of_metricFixedPoint_germ

items.label: inverseCenterDerivative_smul_metricReservedTopCoefficient
items.statement:
Supporting fact: multiplying the predecessor coefficient by the inverse
center derivative gives exactly the successor reserved-top coefficient.
items.title: inverseCenterDerivative_smul_metricReservedTopCoefficient

items.label: inverseCenter_add_metricOrderOneSourceIncrement
items.statement:
Supporting fact: adding the transported source increment reaches the inverse
center of the translated output point.
items.title: inverseCenter_add_metricOrderOneSourceIncrement

items.label: inverseCenter_dist_scale_le
items.statement:
**(A.1) Change-of-variables scale bound.**  The inverse center map `Ψ = d.inverseCenter ζ`
contracts distances by the factor `c = lower⁻¹`: `dist (Ψ y) (Ψ y') ≤ lower⁻¹ · dist y y'`.  This is
the geometric source of the `c·x` self-similarity in the radius-envelope recurrence.
items.title: inverseCenter_dist_scale_le

items.label: isClosed_metricSlopeSection
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the uniform slope constraint cuts out a closed subset of
the bounded continuous section space.
items.title: isClosed_metricSlopeSection

items.label: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_atomic_split_of_contDiff
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the order-`m` derivative of the center-coordinate
remainder splits into its atomic branch and the non-atomic Faà-di-Bruno sum under exactly
`C^m` regularity.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_atomic_split_of_contDiff

items.label: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_residual_contDiff
items.statement:
Supporting fact: under exactly `C^m` regularity and `m ≥ 2`, the
doubled-filter residual in the center-coordinate reserved-top-order split is `C¹`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_residual_contDiff

items.label: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_residual_continuous
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the doubled-filter residual in the center-coordinate
reserved-top-order split is continuous.  Every retained ordered finpartition has length below
`m`, so its outer jet and all inner pair-map jets vary continuously under `ContDiff ℝ m ζ`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_residual_continuous

items.label: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_residual_continuous_of_previousOrder
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the center-coordinate doubled-filter residual is
continuous using only the previous-order regularity of the graph.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_residual_continuous_of_previousOrder

items.label: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_split
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the stronger `C^(m+1)` center-coordinate
reserved-top-order split is a compatibility wrapper around
`iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_split_of_contDiff`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_split

items.label: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_split_of_contDiff
items.statement:
Supporting fact: under exactly `C^m` regularity and `m ≥ 2`, the
order-`m` derivative of the center-coordinate remainder is the sum of its atomic branch,
the center fiber cocycle on `iteratedDeriv m ζ`, and a residual involving only ordered
finpartitions of length neither `1` nor `m`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_center_remainder_length_one_split_of_contDiff

items.label: iteratedDeriv_clm_comp_left
items.statement:
The `m`-th iterated derivative of `L ∘ ζ` at `u` is `L` applied to the `m`-th iterated
derivative of `ζ` at `u`, whenever `ζ` is `Cᵐ` at `u`.  Follows from
`ContinuousLinearMap.iteratedFDeriv_comp_left` plus the definition of `iteratedDeriv` as the
diagonal `fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)` of `iteratedFDeriv`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_clm_comp_left

items.label: iteratedDeriv_eq_iteratedFDeriv_ones
items.statement:
Definitional: the scalar iterated derivative is the all-ones evaluation of the
multilinear iterated derivative.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_eq_iteratedFDeriv_ones

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_atomic_at_origin
items.statement:
**Metric fiber Faà-di-Bruno, origin specialization.**  At the origin, the general
atomic split is obtained by direct evaluation.  The statement keeps the full outer
`iteratedFDeriv` atomic term; reducing it to `derivFiber` requires an additional germ
hypothesis and is intentionally a separate consequence.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_atomic_at_origin

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_atomic_split
items.statement:
**Metric fiber Faà-di-Bruno, general-`u` atomic split.**  The order-`m` iterated
derivative of the fiber remainder `g u = (R (u, ζ u)).2` splits into the atomic top term
plus the Faà-di-Bruno remainder over all non-atomic ordered finpartitions (`c.length ≠ m`).

The atomic term is the FULL chain-rule value `iteratedFDeriv ℝ m (Prod.snd ∘ d.R) (pair u)`
on the diagonal `fun _ ↦ 1` (equivalently `(fderiv ℝ g u) (iteratedDeriv m pair u)`,
which expands to `(∂₁R(u,ζu)) • 1 + derivFiber d ζ u (iteratedDeriv m ζ u)`).  The `∂₁R`
slot is retained because it does **not** vanish for general `u`; use
`iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_atomic_at_origin` for the spec's `derivFiber`-only form at
the origin.  This compatibility form retains the successor-order regularity budget used by
existing callers and delegates to `iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_atomic_split_of_contDiff`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_atomic_split

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_atomic_split_of_contDiff
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the order-`m` derivative of the metric fiber remainder
splits into its atomic branch and the non-atomic Faà-di-Bruno sum under exactly `C^m`
regularity. In particular, constructing this split does not presuppose `C^(m+1)` regularity
of the graph.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_atomic_split_of_contDiff

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_eq_zero_of_pair_notMem_tsupport
items.statement: Off the graph-support, every iterated derivative of the fiber remainder vanishes.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_eq_zero_of_pair_notMem_tsupport

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_residual_contDiff
items.statement:
Supporting fact: under exactly `C^m` regularity and `m ≥ 2`, the
doubled-filter residual in the stable-coordinate reserved-top-order split is `C¹`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_residual_contDiff

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_residual_continuous
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the residual sum of `iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_split` (over ordered
finpartitions of length neither `1` nor `m`) is a continuous function of `u`.  Every such
finpartition has `length < m` (as in `iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_remainder_continuous`),
so the identical continuity argument applies to the doubled filter.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_residual_continuous

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_residual_continuous_of_previousOrder
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the stable-coordinate doubled-filter residual is
continuous using only the previous-order regularity of the graph.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_residual_continuous_of_previousOrder

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_split
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the stronger reserved-top-order split of the fiber remainder (`m ≥ 2`).  The order-`m` iterated
derivative of the fiber remainder `g u = (R (u, ζ u)).2` splits into

  `iteratedDeriv m g u = ATOMIC(m)  +  derivFiber d ζ u (iteratedDeriv m ζ u)  +  RESIDUAL(u)`,

where `ATOMIC(m) = iteratedFDeriv ℝ m (snd ∘ R) (pair u)` on the diagonal first-jet is `W`-free,
the middle term is the *fiber cocycle term* carrying `W = iteratedDeriv m ζ`, and `RESIDUAL(u)` is
the Faà-di-Bruno sum over ordered finpartitions of length **neither `1` nor `m`** — hence every
part has size `≤ m − 1`, so the residual is built purely from `≤ (m−1)`-order jets of `ζ`.  This is
the split the reserved-top-order recurrence needs: the `derivFiber · W` term moves into the
contracted operator, and only the `≤ (m−1)`-jet residual is left to bound by `η · |s|`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_split

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_split_of_contDiff
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the reserved-top-order split of the fiber remainder under
exactly `C^m` regularity.  For `m ≥ 2`, the order-`m` iterated derivative of
`u ↦ (d.R (u, ζ u)).2` is the sum of the atomic branch, the fiber cocycle applied to
`iteratedDeriv m ζ`, and the residual over ordered finpartitions of length neither `1` nor `m`.
Thus the residual depends only on jets of `ζ` of order at most `m - 1`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_length_one_split_of_contDiff

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_remainder_continuous
items.statement:
Helper for the metric fiber Faà-di-Bruno leaf: the Faà-di-Bruno remainder (sum over
non-atomic ordered finpartitions) is a continuous function of `u`.  Uses only that the
fiber slice is `Cᵐ` (from `m ≤ d.nu`): each summand is a continuous order-`c.length`
(`< m`) multilinear jet composed with the continuous `pair`, evaluated at a continuously
varying tuple of iterated `pair`-derivatives of orders `c.partSize j ≤ m`.  No `C¹` control
on the remainder itself is assumed.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fiber_remainder_remainder_continuous

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_cocycle_solved
items.statement:
**Solved cocycle recurrence for the top iterated-derivative section.**  Dividing the undivided
master identity `iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_master_identity` by `(Φ′u)^m ≠ 0`, the top jet
`W (Φ u) = iteratedDeriv m ζ (Φ u)` is expressed as `(Φ′u)⁻ᵐ` times the linear self-reference
`L (W u)` plus the fiber remainder derivative and minus the (strictly lower order) Faà-di-Bruno
`ζ`-remainder.  Requires `ζ ∈ Cᵐ` (`hprev`), `m ≤ d.nu`, and `C¹`-regularity of `ζ` for the
nonvanishing of `Φ′`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_cocycle_solved

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_equation_atomic_split
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the fixed-graph invariance equation transports the
Faà-di-Bruno atomic split from `ζ ∘ centerMap` to the differentiated metric right-hand side.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_equation_atomic_split

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_equation_solved_atomic
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the solved atomic split can be transported through the
fixed-graph equation, replacing `ζ ∘ centerMap` by the metric right-hand side.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_equation_solved_atomic

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_master_identity
items.statement:
Master differentiated identity for the metric fixed graph.  Differentiating the fixed-point
equation `ζ ∘ Φ = L ∘ ζ + g` (Φ := centerMap ζ, g u := (R (u,ζu)).2) `m` times and isolating the
Faà-di-Bruno atomic term gives, after solving for `S (Φ u)` (Φ′ ≠ 0 is NOT needed here — this is the
un-divided form):
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_master_identity

items.label: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_reservedTop_affine_split
items.statement:
Supporting fact: for orders at least two, the differentiated fixed-graph
equation is affine in the reserved top derivative.  Its linear part is the complete fiber
coefficient with negative center feedback, while `metricReservedTopForcing` contains only
lower-order graph jets.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_fixedGraph_reservedTop_affine_split

items.label: iteratedDeriv_hasCompactSupport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: every iterated derivative of a compactly supported scalar
curve remains compactly supported.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_hasCompactSupport

items.label: iteratedDeriv_pair_eq_of_two_le
items.statement:
Supporting fact: for `m ≥ 2`, the order-`m` iterated derivative of the pair map `pair y = (y, ζ y)` at `u` is
`(0, iteratedDeriv m ζ u)`: the first (`id`) component's `m`-th derivative vanishes for `m ≥ 2`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_pair_eq_of_two_le

items.label: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_atomic_split
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the order-`m` iterated derivative of the
composition `ζ ∘ (centerMap ζ)` splits into the isolated atomic top term
`(deriv Φ u)^m • iteratedDeriv m ζ (Φ u)` plus the Faà-di-Bruno remainder over all
non-atomic ordered finpartitions (`c.length ≠ m`).
items.title: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_atomic_split

items.label: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_length_one_residual_contDiff
items.statement:
Supporting fact: under exactly `C^r` regularity and `r ≥ 2`, the doubled-filter
residual from `ζ ∘ centerMap` in the reserved-top affine forcing is `C¹`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_length_one_residual_contDiff

items.label: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_length_one_residual_continuous_of_previousOrder
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the graph-composition doubled-filter residual is
continuous using only the previous-order regularity of the graph.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_length_one_residual_continuous_of_previousOrder

items.label: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_remainder_continuous
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the Faà-di-Bruno remainder (sum over non-atomic
ordered finpartitions) is a continuous function of `u`.  Uses only that `ζ` and `Φ = centerMap ζ`
are `Cᵐ`: each summand is a continuous order-`c.length` (`< m`) multilinear jet of `ζ` composed
with the continuous `Φ`, evaluated at a continuously varying tuple of iterated `Φ`-derivatives of
orders `c.partSize j ≤ m`.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_remainder_continuous

items.label: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_remainder_norm_bound_on_compact
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the Faà-di-Bruno remainder has a uniform norm bound on
every compact set of center coordinates.  This is the boundedness interface needed before a
remainder term can be inserted into a bounded top-section operator.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_remainder_norm_bound_on_compact

items.label: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_solved_atomic
items.statement:
Supporting fact: when the center-map derivative is nonzero, the atomic
Faà-di-Bruno split can be solved for the top iterated derivative of the graph.
items.title: iteratedDeriv_zeta_comp_centerMap_solved_atomic

items.label: linearRate_add_epsilon_le_metricGraphTransformRate
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the linear-plus-fiber coefficient `linearRate + epsilon` is
bounded by the full metric transform rate.  This is `le_self_add` on the opaque rate (the trailing
`(linearRate * slope + epsilon) * lower⁻¹ * epsilon` summand is nonnegative), exposed here as a named
lemma so downstream leaves can bridge the combined operator norm `‖L + derivFiber‖ ≤ linearRate +
epsilon` to the certified `< 1` contraction factor without unfolding the (unexposed) rate.
items.title: linearRate_add_epsilon_le_metricGraphTransformRate

items.label: linearRate_add_epsilon_le_metricGraphTransformRate_real
items.statement:
The real-cast form of `linearRate_add_epsilon_le_metricGraphTransformRate`, ready for the
leaf-level operator-norm bridge: `(linearRate : ℝ) + epsilon ≤ (metricGraphTransformRate …)`.
items.title: linearRate_add_epsilon_le_metricGraphTransformRate_real

items.label: lipschitzWith_invFun_centerProjection
items.statement:
The inverse of the center coordinate along a graph has Lipschitz constant
given by the reciprocal center lower bound.
items.title: lipschitzWith_invFun_centerProjection

items.label: metricCenterAtomicEvaluation_contDiff_one
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the center-coordinate order-`r` atomic evaluation in
`metricReservedTopForcing` is `C¹` when `r ≥ 2`, `r + 1 ≤ d.nu`, and `ζ` is `C^r`.
items.title: metricCenterAtomicEvaluation_contDiff_one

items.label: metricCenterAtomicEvaluation_continuous_of_previousOrder
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the order-`r` center-coordinate atomic evaluation is
continuous under the non-circular assumptions `r ≤ d.nu` and `ζ ∈ C^(r-1)`.
items.title: metricCenterAtomicEvaluation_continuous_of_previousOrder

items.label: metricCenterMapRemainder_uniform
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the center change of variables has a globally
source-uniform first-order Taylor remainder.
items.title: metricCenterMapRemainder_uniform

items.label: metricCenterMap_add_inverseCenterIncrement
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the inverse-center increment transports the perturbed
output coordinate exactly back to the corresponding source coordinate.
items.title: metricCenterMap_add_inverseCenterIncrement

items.label: metricCenterMap_deriv_eq_one_of_graph_notMem_tsupport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: off the graph trace of the remainder support, the metric
center map has derivative one.
items.title: metricCenterMap_deriv_eq_one_of_graph_notMem_tsupport

items.label: metricCenterMap_eq_self_of_graph_notMem_tsupport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: off the graph trace of the remainder support, the metric
center map is the identity.
items.title: metricCenterMap_eq_self_of_graph_notMem_tsupport

items.label: metricCenterMap_inverseCenter
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the center map cancels the inverse center map in output
coordinates.
items.title: metricCenterMap_inverseCenter

items.label: metricCenterStableMap_apply
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the metric center-stable map has the expected coordinate
formula on a graph point.
items.title: metricCenterStableMap_apply

items.label: metricCenterStableMap_contDiff
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a smooth metric remainder makes the represented map
smooth of the same finite order.
items.title: metricCenterStableMap_contDiff

items.label: metricCenterStableMap_eq
items.statement: The metric center-stable map is the pointwise sum of its linear block and remainder.
items.title: metricCenterStableMap_eq

items.label: metricCenterStableMap_hasFDerivAt_of_zeroDerivative
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a zero derivative of the metric remainder gives the
center-stable derivative of the represented map.
items.title: metricCenterStableMap_hasFDerivAt_of_zeroDerivative

items.label: metricCenterStableMap_zero
items.statement: Supporting fact: the represented metric map fixes the origin.
items.title: metricCenterStableMap_zero

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_bunching
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a fixed metric graph is finite-smooth when the metric
transform satisfies finite-order bunching at every order through its declared smoothness.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_bunching

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_holonomicCertificate
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a holonomic top-section certificate upgrades a metric fixed
graph to the declared finite smoothness order.  The proof uses the scalar successor criterion at
each order and does not infer holonomicity from metric contraction alone.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_of_holonomicCertificate

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_one_of_orderOneBunching
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the metric graph-transform fixed graph is continuously differentiable
under the order-one bunching inequality, without assuming differentiability in the construction
of its canonical slope.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_one_of_orderOneBunching

items.label: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_two_of_orderTwoBunching
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the order-two derivative section upgrades the metric fixed
graph from `C¹` to `C²`.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_contDiff_two_of_orderTwoBunching

items.label: metricFixedGraph_deriv_eq_orderOneSlope
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the derivative of the fixed graph is the canonical
continuous slope field selected by the order-one contraction.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_deriv_eq_orderOneSlope

items.label: metricFixedGraph_hasCompactSupport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a fixed metric graph has compactly supported stable
components.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_hasCompactSupport

items.label: metricFixedGraph_hasDerivAt_orderOne
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the canonical fixed slope is the derivative of the fixed
Lipschitz graph at every center.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_hasDerivAt_orderOne

items.label: metricFixedGraph_higherOrderDerivativeSection
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: at every predecessor order `m ≥ 2`, successor bunching produces a
continuous derivative section for `iteratedDeriv m` of the metric fixed graph.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_higherOrderDerivativeSection

items.label: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_bunching
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure (Finite-smooth invariant graph under an explicit stable contraction):
for every finite order satisfying the metric bunching inequalities, the
fixed graph has the continuous holonomic top sections required by the finite-jet successor
argument.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_holonomicCertificate_of_bunching

items.label: metricFixedGraph_invariant
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a metric transform fixed graph satisfies the invariant
equation for the represented center-stable map.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_invariant

items.label: metricFixedGraph_orderTwoDerivativeSection
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: under the order-one and order-two bunching inequalities, the first
derivative of the metric fixed graph has the continuous canonical reserved order-two derivative
section.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_orderTwoDerivativeSection

items.label: metricFixedGraph_topSection_of_core
items.statement:
**Conditional export.**  Given the metric top-section core, the frozen holonomic
`topSection` obligation holds at every order `1 ≤ r ≤ d.nu`.  This wires the core through the
cycle-safe `MetricTopSectionDerivativeBridge` reduction; the only outstanding obligation of
Claim 1 is the construction of `hcore`.
items.title: metricFixedGraph_topSection_of_core

items.label: metricGraphTransformRate_coe
items.statement:
Supporting fact: coercing `metricGraphTransformRate` to `ℝ` gives its
three-term scalar expansion.
items.title: metricGraphTransformRate_coe

items.label: metricInverseCenter_centerMap
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the inverse center map cancels the center map in source
coordinates.
items.title: metricInverseCenter_centerMap

items.label: metricIteratedDeriv_hasDerivAt_higherOrder
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the canonical differentiated reserved-top fixed section is
the pointwise derivative of the predecessor iterated derivative.
items.title: metricIteratedDeriv_hasDerivAt_higherOrder

items.label: metricOrderOneCenterIncrement_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the center output increment is the source increment times the
candidate secant denominator, plus the center Taylor residual.
items.title: metricOrderOneCenterIncrement_eq

items.label: metricOrderOneDenominator_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the split denominator equals the full derivative of the
center component on the candidate direction `(1, b u)`.
items.title: metricOrderOneDenominator_eq

items.label: metricOrderOneDenominator_fixedSlope_eq_centerMap_deriv
items.statement:
Supporting fact: on the canonical fixed slope, the rational denominator is
the derivative of the center change of variables.
items.title: metricOrderOneDenominator_fixedSlope_eq_centerMap_deriv

items.label: metricOrderOneDenominator_lower
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the order-one scalar denominator is bounded away from
zero by the certified center lower bound.
items.title: metricOrderOneDenominator_lower

items.label: metricOrderOneDenominator_ne_zero
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the order-one scalar denominator never vanishes on the
closed slope ball.
items.title: metricOrderOneDenominator_ne_zero

items.label: metricOrderOneDenominator_smul_slopeValue
items.statement:
Supporting fact: multiplying a slope value by its nonzero denominator recovers
the corresponding numerator.
items.title: metricOrderOneDenominator_smul_slopeValue

items.label: metricOrderOneDenominator_smul_slopeValue_sub_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: after multiplying by the first candidate denominator, the
slope-value difference has only one inverse denominator.
items.title: metricOrderOneDenominator_smul_slopeValue_sub_eq

items.label: metricOrderOneDenominator_sub_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: subtracting two candidate denominators cancels the
first-slot contribution and leaves only the center fiber derivative on the slope difference.
items.title: metricOrderOneDenominator_sub_eq

items.label: metricOrderOneDifferenceCoefficient_apply
items.statement:
Supporting fact: application of the order-one difference coefficient
exposes its fiber term and fixed-output center feedback.
items.title: metricOrderOneDifferenceCoefficient_apply

items.label: metricOrderOneDifferenceCoefficient_apply_norm_le
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the exact order-one difference coefficient has the sharp
pointwise bound `metricGraphTransformRate * lower⁻¹`, paid for by the fixed slope output bound.
items.title: metricOrderOneDifferenceCoefficient_apply_norm_le

items.label: metricOrderOneDifferenceCoefficient_fixed_eq_centerDeriv_smul_reserved
items.statement:
Supporting fact: at the canonical fixed slope, the exact rational difference
coefficient is the center derivative times the reserved order-two coefficient.
items.title: metricOrderOneDifferenceCoefficient_fixed_eq_centerDeriv_smul_reserved

items.label: metricOrderOneDifferenceCoefficient_translated_uniform
items.statement:
Supporting fact: translating the canonical fixed slope changes the exact
difference coefficient uniformly little in operator norm.
items.title: metricOrderOneDifferenceCoefficient_translated_uniform

items.label: metricOrderOneFixedSlope_fixed
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the canonical order-one slope is fixed by the slope
operator.
items.title: metricOrderOneFixedSlope_fixed

items.label: metricOrderOneFixedSlope_hasDerivAt_orderTwo
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the canonical reserved order-two section is the derivative
of the canonical fixed slope at every source center.
items.title: metricOrderOneFixedSlope_hasDerivAt_orderTwo

items.label: metricOrderOneFixedSlope_value
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the fixed slope satisfies the explicit inverse-center
denominator/numerator equation at every output center.
items.title: metricOrderOneFixedSlope_value

items.label: metricOrderOneGraphDerivative_eq_smul
items.statement:
Supporting fact: on a nonzero graph increment, the derivative of `R` on the
actual graph chord is the increment times the derivative on the translated secant direction.
items.title: metricOrderOneGraphDerivative_eq_smul

items.label: metricOrderOneGraphRemainder_spec
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the remainder difference is its linearization on the actual
graph increment plus the named two-point Taylor residual.
items.title: metricOrderOneGraphRemainder_spec

items.label: metricOrderOneGraphRemainder_uniform
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the two-point remainder of `R` along every admissible
Lipschitz graph is uniformly `o(|s|)` in the scalar graph increment.
items.title: metricOrderOneGraphRemainder_uniform

items.label: metricOrderOneNumerator_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the split numerator equals the linear stable term plus
the full remainder derivative on the candidate direction `(1, b u)`.
items.title: metricOrderOneNumerator_eq

items.label: metricOrderOneNumerator_eq_denominator_smul_fixedValue
items.statement:
Supporting fact: at a fixed slope section, the numerator equals the
candidate denominator times the fixed output over the corresponding center coordinate.
items.title: metricOrderOneNumerator_eq_denominator_smul_fixedValue

items.label: metricOrderOneNumerator_sub_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: subtracting two candidate numerators cancels the
first-slot contribution and leaves `L + derivFiber` on the slope difference.
items.title: metricOrderOneNumerator_sub_eq

items.label: metricOrderOneRawDefect_decomposition
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the raw defect splits into the denominator-cancelled slope
difference and the two components of the graph Taylor remainder.
items.title: metricOrderOneRawDefect_decomposition

items.label: metricOrderOneRawDefect_inverseRecurrence
items.statement:
Supporting fact: uniform smallness of the graph Taylor remainder turns the
raw identity into the affine recurrence required by the radius-envelope theorem.
items.title: metricOrderOneRawDefect_inverseRecurrence

items.label: metricOrderOneRawDefect_isLittleO
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the raw first-order defect is little-o of its increment at
every base point.
items.title: metricOrderOneRawDefect_isLittleO

items.label: metricOrderOneRawDefect_locallyUniformlyBounded
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the order-one raw defect is uniformly bounded on a fixed
neighborhood of the zero increment.
items.title: metricOrderOneRawDefect_locallyUniformlyBounded

items.label: metricOrderOneRawDefect_source_identity
items.statement:
Supporting fact: at the inverse-center increment, the transported raw defect
is exactly the source increment times the difference between the secant and fixed slope fields.
items.title: metricOrderOneRawDefect_source_identity

items.label: metricOrderOneRawDefect_zero
items.statement: Supporting fact: the order-one raw defect vanishes at the zero increment.
items.title: metricOrderOneRawDefect_zero

items.label: metricOrderOneSlopeBoundedSection_apply
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the bundled slope transform evaluates by the explicit
inverse-center denominator/numerator formula.
items.title: metricOrderOneSlopeBoundedSection_apply

items.label: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_apply
items.statement:
Supporting fact: evaluation of the closed-ball slope operator is the
explicit slope-transform value.
items.title: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_apply

items.label: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_apply_centerMap_eq_frozen
items.statement:
Supporting fact: source-coordinate evaluation of the slope transform is
the frozen rational value at the candidate direction.
items.title: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_apply_centerMap_eq_frozen

items.label: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_contractingWith
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the real bunching inequality makes the closed-ball slope
operator a `ContractingWith` map.
items.title: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_contractingWith

items.label: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_dist_apply_le
items.statement:
Supporting infrastructure: the closed-ball order-one slope operator has the precise pointwise
contraction factor `metricGraphTransformRate * lower⁻¹`.
items.title: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_dist_apply_le

items.label: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_sub_fixed_apply_centerMap
items.statement:
Supporting fact: at `y = centerMap zeta u`, subtracting a fixed slope
section from the transformed candidate is the difference coefficient applied to `c u - b u`.
items.title: metricOrderOneSlopeOperator_sub_fixed_apply_centerMap

items.label: metricOrderOneSlopeValue_dist_le_source
items.statement:
Supporting fact: at a fixed output coordinate, the slope transform obeys
the exact full-rate estimate against the input difference at the inverse center.
items.title: metricOrderOneSlopeValue_dist_le_source

items.label: metricOrderOneSlopeValue_sub_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the difference of two slope-transform values separates
into a numerator difference and an inverse-denominator difference.
items.title: metricOrderOneSlopeValue_sub_eq

items.label: metricOrderOneSourceIncrement_ne_zero
items.statement:
Supporting fact: a nonzero output increment has a nonzero inverse-center
source increment.
items.title: metricOrderOneSourceIncrement_ne_zero

items.label: metricOrderOneStableIncrement_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: fixed-graph invariance transports the stable output increment
to the source secant numerator, up to the stable Taylor residual.
items.title: metricOrderOneStableIncrement_eq

items.label: metricOrderOneVariableIncrement_residual_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the variable-increment graph secant differs from the
order-one slope value by the two Taylor residuals.  The source increment is the inverse-center
increment selected by `(y,t)`, so no fixed-increment or differentiability hypothesis is hidden in
this identity.
items.title: metricOrderOneVariableIncrement_residual_eq

items.label: metricOrderOneVariableIncrement_residual_eq_center
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the center-coordinate residual scalar can be eliminated from
the variable-increment identity.  The resulting expression exposes both Taylor components and is
the form used for uniform residual estimates.
items.title: metricOrderOneVariableIncrement_residual_eq_center

items.label: metricOrderTwoBaseVariation_eq_frozenDifference
items.statement:
Supporting fact: for a fixed slope, the base variation is exactly the
source increment of the frozen rational value at the translated stable direction.
items.title: metricOrderTwoBaseVariation_eq_frozenDifference

items.label: metricOrderTwoBaseVariation_uniform
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the fixed-slope base variation has a source-uniform
first-order expansion given by the scaled reserved order-two forcing.
items.title: metricOrderTwoBaseVariation_uniform

items.label: metricOrderTwoFixedSection_centerDerivativeEquation
items.statement:

items.title: metricOrderTwoFixedSection_centerDerivativeEquation

items.label: metricOrderTwoFixedSection_sourceEquation

Supporting fact: the canonical order-two section satisfies the reserved
affine equation in source coordinates.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFixedSection_sourceEquation

items.label: metricOrderTwoFixedSlope_increment_decomposition
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the fixed-slope increment is the exact rational principal
term plus the named source-coordinate base variation.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFixedSlope_increment_decomposition

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenDenominator_eq

items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenDenominator_eq

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenDenominator_hasDerivAt
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the frozen denominator derivative is the center
coordinate of the diagonal second derivative of `R`.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenDenominator_hasDerivAt

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenDenominator_lower
items.statement:
Supporting fact: every frozen denominator over the closed slope ball is
bounded below by the certified center factor.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenDenominator_lower

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenDenominator_ne_zero
items.statement:
Supporting fact: every frozen denominator over the closed slope ball is
nonzero.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenDenominator_ne_zero

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenNumerator_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: freezing a slope candidate at its value over `u` recovers
the ordinary candidate numerator at `u`.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenNumerator_eq

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenNumerator_hasDerivAt
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the frozen numerator derivative is the stable
coordinate of the diagonal second derivative of `R`.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenNumerator_hasDerivAt

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenRDerivative_hasDerivAt
items.statement:
Supporting fact: along the fixed graph, differentiating the frozen
first derivative of `R` produces its diagonal second derivative.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenRDerivative_hasDerivAt

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_contDiffAt
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the frozen rational slope is jointly C¹ at every source
and every stable direction in the closed slope ball.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_contDiffAt

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_eq_linear_of_notMem_tsupport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: off the support of the smooth remainder, the frozen
rational slope is just the linear stable map.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_eq_linear_of_notMem_tsupport

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_fixed
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the frozen rational value at the fixed slope direction is
the fixed slope at the corresponding output center.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_fixed

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_hasDerivAt
items.statement:
Supporting fact: with the stable direction frozen at the canonical fixed
slope, the rational slope value has derivative equal to the center derivative times the
order-two reserved forcing.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_hasDerivAt

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_hasDerivAt_sourceDerivative
items.statement:
Supporting fact: each frozen source slice has derivative given by the
source partial derivative whenever its direction lies in the closed slope ball.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_hasDerivAt_sourceDerivative

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_translated_remainder_eq
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the order-one Taylor remainder of a translated frozen
slope slice is its affine source-partial error.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenSlopeValue_translated_remainder_eq

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenSourceDerivative_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport
items.statement:
Supporting fact: off the support of the smooth remainder, the frozen
rational slope has zero source partial derivative.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenSourceDerivative_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport

items.label: metricOrderTwoFrozenSourceDerivative_fixed
items.statement:
Supporting fact: at the canonical fixed direction, the frozen source
partial derivative is the center derivative times the reserved order-two forcing.
items.title: metricOrderTwoFrozenSourceDerivative_fixed

items.label: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_decomposition
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the output raw defect is the rational coefficient applied
to the inverse-center raw defect, plus the named base-variation residual.
items.title: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_decomposition

items.label: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_inverseRecurrence
items.statement:
Supporting fact: uniform smallness of the order-two residual turns the
raw identity into the inverse-center affine recurrence used by the radius envelope.
items.title: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_inverseRecurrence

items.label: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_isLittleO
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the raw defect of the canonical fixed slope relative to

items.title: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_isLittleO

items.label: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_locallyUniformlyBounded
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the order-two raw defect is uniformly bounded on a fixed
neighborhood of the zero increment.
items.title: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_locallyUniformlyBounded

items.label: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_zero
items.statement: Supporting fact: the order-two raw defect vanishes at zero increment.
items.title: metricOrderTwoRawDefect_zero

items.label: metricOrderTwoResidual_error_decomposition

Supporting fact: the residual is the sum of the frozen-base Taylor error,
the translated-coefficient error, and the center-map Taylor error.
items.title: metricOrderTwoResidual_error_decomposition

items.label: metricOrderTwoResidual_uniform
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the complete order-two residual is uniformly little
compared with the output-center increment.
items.title: metricOrderTwoResidual_uniform

items.label: metricOrderTwoTranslatedSlope_apply
items.statement:
Supporting fact: evaluating the translated slope candidate shifts its source

items.label: metricReservedTopAffineRemainder_uniform

Supporting fact: the affine remainder in the differentiated reserved-top

items.label: metricReservedTopCoefficientSection_apply

Supporting fact: evaluation of the bundled coefficient is the original

items.title: metricReservedTopCoefficientSection_apply

items.label: metricReservedTopCoefficient_apply

Supporting fact: application of `metricReservedTopCoefficient` exposes the

items.label: metricReservedTopCoefficient_apply_norm_le

Supporting fact: on a fixed graph, the complete reserved-top-order
coefficient is bounded by the full metric transform rate; its trailing rate term absorbs the
center feedback using the sharp fixed-graph Lipschitz constant.
items.title: metricReservedTopCoefficient_apply_norm_le

items.label: metricReservedTopCoefficient_contDiff_one_of_previousOrder
items.statement:
Supporting fact: the reserved-top coefficient at every order at least two is

items.label: metricReservedTopCoefficient_continuous

items.label: operator_fiber_cocycle_norm_le
items.statement:
The pointwise Lipschitz bound for the **combined** fiber-cocycle operator
`M(u) := L + derivFiber u`:  `‖(Φ′u)⁻ᵐ • (L + derivFiber u) w‖ ≤ ((linearRate + epsilon)·lower⁻ᵐ)·‖w‖`.
The `L`-part reuses `operator_linear_part_norm_le`; the `derivFiber`-part uses `‖derivFiber‖ ≤ ε`
(`norm_derivFiber_le`) and `|(Φ′u)⁻ᵐ| ≤ lower⁻ᵐ` (`centerMap_deriv_inv_pow_abs_le`).
items.title: operator_fiber_cocycle_norm_le

items.label: operator_fiber_cocycle_norm_le_rate
items.statement:
The combined fiber-cocycle operator is bounded by the **metric transform rate**:
`‖(Φ′u)⁻ᵐ • (L + derivFiber u) w‖ ≤ (rate · lower⁻ᵐ) · ‖w‖`, where
`rate = metricGraphTransformRate …`.  Chains `operator_fiber_cocycle_norm_le` through
`linearRate_add_epsilon_le_metricGraphTransformRate_real`.  The coefficient `rate · lower⁻ᵐ` is
`< 1` by `bunching_linear_factor_lt_one`.
items.title: operator_fiber_cocycle_norm_le_rate

items.label: operator_linear_part_norm_le
items.statement:
The pointwise linear-part Lipschitz bound for the fixed-section operator, stated with the exact
linear coefficient `linearRate` (which bounds `‖L‖` via `d.hL`):
`‖(Φ′u)⁻ᵐ • L w‖ ≤ (linearRate · lower⁻ᵐ) · ‖w‖`.  Combines `‖L w‖ ≤ linearRate · ‖w‖` (from `d.hL`)
with `|(Φ′u)⁻ᵐ| ≤ lower⁻ᵐ` (from `centerMap_deriv_lower_bound`).  Since
`linearRate ≤ metricGraphTransformRate …` (monotonicity of the rate, all summands nonnegative), this
also bounds the operator by `rate · lower⁻ᵐ`, the factor `bunching_linear_factor_lt_one` proves
`< 1`.
items.title: operator_linear_part_norm_le

items.label: subtracted_cocycle_changeOfVariables
items.statement:
**(A.2) Subtracted-cocycle change-of-variables secant identity (keystone).**  Given the value
cocycle in `Rem`-form — `∀ w, W (Φ w) = (Φ′w)⁻ᵐ • L (W w) + Rem w`, with `W := iteratedDeriv m ζ`,
`Φ := d.centerMap ζ` and `Rem : ℝ → X` opaque (the `(C)` lower-order bucket) — the translation secant
of `W` between `y` and `y'` decomposes as the difference of the `(Φ′)⁻ᵐ • L`-self-references at the
inverse-center preimages `Ψ y, Ψ y'` plus the difference of remainders.  Uses only `Φ (Ψ y) = y`
(right inverse of the bijective center map).  This exhibits the exact `p·F(c·x) + (lower order)`
SHAPE — the self-reference term is `L` applied to `W` sampled at points separated by
`≤ lower⁻¹ · dist y y'` (via `inverseCenter_dist_scale_le`), and the remainder difference is the
lower-order forcing — WITHOUT discharging the `(C)` estimate (which stays inside the opaque `Rem`).
items.title: subtracted_cocycle_changeOfVariables

items.label: topSectionWitness_at_of_core
